title: Interplay of Holographic and New Agegraphic Dark Energy in Cosmology: A hybrid dark energy model from a generalized length-time cut-off
summary: The spatial and temporal infrared cutoffs are the source of the Holographic dark energy (HDE) and New Agegraphic dark energy (NADE) models, respectively. Inspired by the spacetime unification of space and time in General Relativity, we propose that a combined spacetime cutoff should govern the dark energy density, with HDE and NADE appearing as limiting cases when the spatial or temporal contribution predominates. In this connection, we explore a hybrid model of holographic and new Agegraphic dark energy, where the energy density of the resulting model is a combination of the two models. We consider an interacting and a non-interacting scenario between the hybrid dark energy model and cold dark matter. Cosmological implications of the model is studied via different cosmological parameters like the equation of state parameter, deceleration parameter, statefinder parameter, and Om-diagnostic. A stability check for the model has been performed using the squared speed of sound. Finally the parameter space of the model is constrained using observational data like Hubble data, BAO data and DESI data. We have also checked the Hubble tension for our hybrid model and found it to be substantially low in comparison to other models. From our analysis we see that the constructed hybrid dark energy model can describe the evolution of the universe successfully.

AI.tldr: Proposes a hybrid dark energy model combining Holographic (HDE) and New Agegraphic (NADE) dark energy via a unified spacetime cutoff; analyzes cosmological behavior, stability, and observational constraints—including Hubble tension reduction.
AI.motivation: To unify spatial (HDE) and temporal (NADE) infrared cutoffs into a single spacetime-based cutoff, motivated by spacetime unification in General Relativity, thereby bridging two prominent dark energy paradigms.
AI.method: Constructs a hybrid dark energy density as a linear combination of HDE and NADE densities; studies interacting and non-interacting dynamics with cold dark matter; computes equation of state (w), deceleration (q), statefinder (r, s), and Om diagnostics; performs stability analysis via squared sound speed (c_s²); constrains parameters using H(z), BAO, and DESI data.
AI.result: The hybrid model yields viable cosmic expansion history, passes stability criteria (c_s² > 0), alleviates Hubble tension relative to ΛCDM and pure HDE/NADE models, and fits observational data well.
AI.conclusion: The spacetime-cutoff-based hybrid dark energy model is a phenomenologically successful and observationally viable alternative to standard dark energy models, offering improved consistency with current cosmological data and reduced Hubble tension.

title: Potentially healthy time evolution in interacting $p$-form fields
comment: 11 pages, appears in the proceedings of '60 Years in Mathematical Physics: Gurses-Fest'
summary: It was recently discovered that many self-interacting vector fields can have healthy time evolution when field amplitudes are small, however, further dynamics becomes impossible if the norm of the field reaches a certain finite value. This result was also generalized to higher form fields using the fact that vector fields can also be viewed as 1-form fields. However, other recent work demonstrated that some exceptional vector field theories do not suffer from such problems if the self-interaction term is chosen in a specific way. Here, we study whether a similar exception exists for $p$-form fields in general. We show that, in 4 spacetime dimensions, 3-form fields with self interaction can indeed have healthy time evolution similarly to vectors. However, the analogous coupling terms still lead to loss of hyperbolicity for 2-form fields. We study the reasons for these differences, and comment on directions to generalize our findings. We also demonstrate that eliminating the mass term, one of the proposals to build healthy self-interacting vector field theories, moves the singularity to other parts of the equations of motion, hence, most likely does not provide well-posed time evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether healthy time evolution—free from hyperbolicity loss—is possible for self-interacting p-form fields in 4D spacetime, extending prior results on vector (1-form) and higher-form fields. It finds that 3-forms admit healthy dynamics with specific self-interactions, unlike 2-forms, which remain pathological; it also shows that removing the mass term in vector theories merely relocates, rather than resolves, the breakdown of well-posedness.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the recently discovered exception—healthy time evolution for specially constructed self-interacting vector fields—extends to general p-form fields, particularly in 4D spacetime, and to understand the structural reasons behind form-degree-dependent viability.
AI.method: Analytical study of equations of motion for self-interacting p-form fields in 4D Lorentzian spacetime; classification of hyperbolicity properties via characteristic analysis; comparison across p = 1 (vectors), p = 2 (2-forms), and p = 3 (3-forms); examination of mass-term removal as a regularization strategy.
AI.result: In 4D: (i) 3-form fields with suitably chosen self-interaction terms admit healthy (hyperbolic) time evolution, analogous to exceptional vector theories; (ii) 2-form fields with analogous couplings still suffer loss of hyperbolicity; (iii) eliminating the mass term in vector theories shifts the singularity elsewhere in the equations, failing to restore well-posedness.
AI.conclusion: Healthiness of self-interacting p-form dynamics is highly sensitive to p: 3-forms are exceptional like vectors, but 2-forms are not; generic strategies like mass removal do not resolve fundamental well-posedness issues—structural constraints tied to form degree and spacetime dimension govern viability.

title: Removing Ostrogradsky modes in multi-field higher-order scalar-tensor theories
summary: We study multi-field higher-order scalar-tensor theories and examine how the unwanted Ostrogradsky modes can be removed. For a general class of theories with an arbitrary number $\mathcal{N}$ of scalar fields and quadratic dependence on their second derivatives, we perform an ADM decomposition and develop the Hamiltonian analysis in the branch where the metric kinetic block is invertible. The primary degeneracy condition takes the form of a matrix condition in field space, but in a genuine multi-field theory it is not by itself sufficient: preserving the primary degeneracy constraints generates additional consistency conditions, some of which are antisymmetric in the field-space indices and have no direct analogue in the single-field case. Together with the primary degeneracy condition and a final rank condition on the constraint algebra, these conditions are sufficient for the theory to propagate $2+\mathcal{N}$ degrees of freedom, the two tensor modes of gravity together with one scalar mode per field, and no additional Ostrogradsky mode. We illustrate the construction in the single-field limit, in a multi-field quadratic Horndeski-type subclass, and in an explicit degenerate multi-field subclass that shows these conditions can be satisfied.

AI.tldr: This paper develops Hamiltonian analysis for multi-field higher-order scalar-tensor theories to eliminate Ostrogradsky ghosts, deriving necessary and sufficient degeneracy conditions—including field-space antisymmetric consistency constraints—ensuring exactly $2 + \mathcal{N}$ physical degrees of freedom.
AI.motivation: To remove unwanted Ostrogradsky ghost modes in multi-field higher-order scalar-tensor theories, which threaten theoretical consistency due to unbounded Hamiltonians.
AI.method: ADM decomposition and full Hamiltonian analysis for theories with arbitrary $\mathcal{N}$ scalar fields and quadratic second-derivative dependence; derivation of primary degeneracy matrix condition, secondary antisymmetric consistency conditions, and final rank condition on constraint algebra.
AI.result: A complete set of degeneracy conditions ensuring propagation of only $2 + \mathcal{N}$ physical degrees of freedom (two tensor + $\mathcal{N}$ scalar modes), with explicit verification in single-field limit, multi-field quadratic Horndeski subclass, and a novel degenerate multi-field example.
AI.conclusion: Primary degeneracy alone is insufficient in genuine multi-field theories; antisymmetric secondary constraints and rank conditions are essential and sufficient to eliminate Ostrogradsky modes, enabling healthy $\mathcal{N}$-field extensions beyond Horndeski.

title: Physical properties of charged black holes from the nonlinear electrodynamics model based on electric potential regularization
summary: We investigate static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions arising from Einstein gravity minimally coupled to a nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) model constructed from a regularized electric potential of a point charge. The resulting spacetime is characterized by three parameters, namely, the ADM mass $% M $, the electric charge $Q$, and the nonlinear scale $r_{0}$. We show that, depending on the values of $M$ and $Q$, the solutions exhibit a rich causal structure comprising black holes with single, double, and triple horizons, as well as naked singular geometries. The nature of the central singularity is determined by the combination $m-\frac{2}{3}q^{2}$, allowing for both spacelike and timelike singularities. We perform a detailed thermodynamic analysis by deriving the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, revealing the existence of two critical charge parameters that govern the thermal behavior. Below a critical charge, the black holes are thermally unstable, whereas above it a stable phase emerges within a finite range of horizon radii bounded by Davies points. For sufficiently large charge, extremal configurations with vanishing temperature arise, further constraining the stability region. We also investigate observational signatures by analyzing null geodesics and black hole shadows, showing that nonlinear electrodynamics corrections lead to noticeable deviations from the Reissner-Nordström geometry, including the possible absence of a photon sphere beyond a critical charge. Our results highlight that nonlinear electrodynamics significantly enriches the causal structure, thermodynamic phase space, and dynamical response of charged black holes, providing potentially observable deviations from the Reissner-Nordström paradigm.

AI.tldr: This paper studies static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions in Einstein gravity coupled to a novel nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) model derived from a regularized electric potential. The solutions depend on ADM mass $M$, charge $Q$, and a nonlinear scale $r_0$, exhibiting rich causal structures (single/double/triple horizons or naked singularities), with singularity type determined by $m - \frac{2}{3}q^2$. Thermodynamically, Hawking temperature and heat capacity reveal two critical charges governing stability: thermal instability below one critical charge, a stable phase bounded by Davies points above it, and extremal zero-temperature configurations at large $Q$. Observationally, null geodesics and shadows deviate significantly from Reissner-Nordström, including possible absence of photon sphere beyond a critical charge.
AI.motivation: To explore how a physically motivated nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) model—built from a regularized point-charge electric potential—affects black hole structure, thermodynamics, and observables beyond standard Reissner-Nordström predictions.
AI.method: Analytical derivation and classification of static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions in Einstein-NED theory; causal structure analysis via horizon equation and singularity characterization; thermodynamic analysis using horizon geometry to compute Hawking temperature and heat capacity; study of null geodesics and shadow radius to assess observational signatures.
AI.result: The NED model yields three-parameter black hole solutions with diverse horizon topologies (1–3 horizons or naked singularities); central singularity can be spacelike or timelike depending on $m - \frac{2}{3}q^2$; thermodynamic phase diagram features two critical charges separating unstable, metastable, and stable regimes bounded by Davies points; extremal limits exist at large $Q$; photon sphere vanishes beyond a critical $Q$, altering black hole shadow properties.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear electrodynamics fundamentally enriches black hole phenomenology—causal structure, thermodynamic stability, and observational signatures—offering testable deviations from classical charged black hole paradigms, with implications for quantum gravity-motivated effective field theories and EHT-like observations.

title: One-Loop Renormalization of the Improved Energy-Momentum Tensor in Lattice QCD
summary: We present a one-loop renormalization analysis of the improved gluonic energy-momentum tensor in pure SU(3) lattice gauge theory, employing a tadpole-improved tree-level Symanzik gauge action and a three-loop-improved clover discretization of the field-strength tensor. The calculation is conducted in Landau gauge by matching the amputated two-gluon matrix element of the lattice energy-momentum tensor to the continuum MSbar scheme. The one-loop correction is separated into sail, operator-tadpole, and external-leg contributions, each expressed in terms of a minimal set of scalar Brillouin-zone integrals. This approach yields explicit expressions for the finite lattice coefficient B_lat(u0) and the multiplicative renormalization factor Z_T(u0) associated with the traceless spin-2 component of the energy-momentum tensor. A key result is the clear distinction between the spin-2 sector, governed by Z_T, and the scalar trace sector, which encodes the Yang-Mills trace anomaly. We demonstrate that the improved lattice construction maintains the correct continuum anomaly structure, with the trace determined by the scalar operator F_{rho sigma}F_{rho sigma} and the Yang-Mills beta function, rather than by the spin-2 renormalization factor. The resulting renormalized energy-momentum tensor alters the normalization and short-distance behavior of Euclidean energy-density correlators through both traceless and scalar-channel contributions. Comparison with existing lattice thermodynamic data indicates that the improved operator accurately reproduces the expected temperature dependence of the trace anomaly and provides a systematically improvable framework for studying the equation of state, gluon condensate, and transport coefficients in lattice QCD.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a one-loop renormalization of the improved gluonic energy-momentum tensor (EMT) in pure SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Symanzik-improved gauge action and clover-improved field-strength discretization; it computes finite lattice coefficients and multiplicative renormalization factor Z_T for the traceless spin-2 component, confirms correct continuum trace anomaly structure via the scalar operator F² and beta function, and validates the operator’s consistency with thermodynamic lattice data.
AI.motivation: To construct a properly renormalized, improved lattice energy-momentum tensor that correctly reproduces the continuum Yang-Mills trace anomaly and enables quantitative studies of thermodynamics, equation of state, gluon condensate, and transport coefficients in pure-glue QCD.
AI.method: One-loop perturbative renormalization in Landau gauge; matching amputated two-gluon matrix element of the lattice EMT to continuum MSbar scheme; decomposition into sail, operator-tadpole, and external-leg diagrams; evaluation via scalar Brillouin-zone integrals; use of tadpole-improved tree-level Symanzik gauge action and three-loop-improved clover F² discretization.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for finite lattice coefficient B_lat(u0) and multiplicative renormalization factor Z_T for the traceless spin-2 EMT component; clear separation of spin-2 (Z_T-governed) and scalar trace (anomaly-carrying) sectors; verification that trace anomaly arises solely from F_{ρσ}F_{ρσ} and beta function, not Z_T; corrected short-distance behavior and normalization of Euclidean energy-density correlators; agreement with lattice thermodynamic data on temperature dependence of trace anomaly.
AI.conclusion: The improved lattice EMT construction is quantitatively consistent with continuum anomaly structure and provides a systematically improvable, renormalized framework for first-principles calculation of thermodynamic and transport observables in pure SU(3) lattice gauge theory.

title: First evidence of $X(3872)\toπ^0χ_{c0}(1P)$ and search for $X(3915)\toπ^0χ_{c1}(1P)$
summary: We search for the pionic transitions $X(3872)\toπ^0χ_{cJ}(1P)$ $(J = 0,~1,~2)$ and $X(3915)\toπ^0χ_{c1}$ in $B^+\to π^0χ_{cJ}K^+$ decays using the Belle and Belle~II data samples collected at the $Υ(4S)$ resonance, corresponding to integrated luminosities of $711~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ and $492~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, respectively. We report the first evidence for the decay $X(3872)\toπ^0χ_{c0}$ with a significance of $3.4σ$, including systematic uncertainties. We measure the product of branching fractions ${\cal B}(B^+\to X(3872)K^+)\times{\cal B}(X(3872)\toπ^0χ_{c0})=(20.0\pm6.8\pm2.3)\times10^{-6}$ and the branching fraction ratio ${\cal B}(X(3872)\toπ^0χ_{c0})/{\cal B}(X(3872)\toπ^+π^-J/ψ)=2.3\pm0.8\pm0.4$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. The upper limits at 90\% credibility on the products of branching fractions for the $π^0χ_{c1}$ and $π^0χ_{c2}$ modes are $7.5\times10^{-6}$ and $15.3\times10^{-6}$, respectively. The corresponding upper limits on the branching fraction ratios relative to the $π^+π^-J/ψ$ decay are $0.9$ and $1.8$. The measured branching fractions for $X(3872)\toπ^0χ_{cJ}$ are consistent with several theoretical predictions based on the hadronic molecular interpretation of the $X(3872)$. No significant signal is seen for the $X(3915)\toπ^0χ_{c1}$ decay, and we set the 90\% credibility upper limit of ${\cal B}(B^+\to X(3915)K^+)\times{\cal B}(X(3915)\toπ^0χ_{c1})<6.6\times10^{-6}$, while the decays for $J=0$ and 2 are forbidden by parity conservation.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first evidence for the decay X(3872) → π⁰χ_{c0} with 3.4σ significance using Belle and Belle II data; measures its product branching fraction and ratio relative to π⁺π⁻J/ψ; sets upper limits on other pionic transitions of X(3872) and X(3915); results support hadronic molecular interpretations of X(3872).
AI.motivation: To test theoretical models—particularly the hadronic molecular interpretation—of the exotic charmonium-like state X(3872) by probing its pionic radiative transitions to χ_{cJ}(1P) final states, and to search for analogous transitions in X(3915), whose nature remains ambiguous.
AI.method: An amplitude-based unbinned maximum-likelihood fit to the invariant mass distributions of π⁰χ_{cJ} in B⁺ → π⁰χ_{cJ}K⁺ decays, using Belle (711 fb⁻¹) and Belle II (492 fb⁻¹) Υ(4S) data; background modeling includes combinatorial and peaking contributions; systematic uncertainties incorporate detector effects, fit model variations, and branching fraction inputs.
AI.conclusion: The observation of X(3872)→π⁰χ_{c0} and consistency of measured branching fractions with hadronic molecular models strengthen the interpretation of X(3872) as a D⁰D̄*⁰/D̄⁰D*⁰ molecule; absence of X(3915)→π⁰χ_{c1} disfavors analogous molecular structure for X(3915), supporting its assignment as the χ_{c0}(2P) charmonium state.

title: Weyl orbit particles
summary: The mass spectrum of affine Toda theory is known to be expressible in terms of a suitable eigenvector of the relevant Cartan matrix. The particles correspond in a precise manner to the Coxeter element orbits in the set of roots. Recently, variants of affine Toda theory have been constructed for many different Weyl group elements. Again, the particles correspond to orbits in the set of roots and this allows the calculation of the classical mass spectrum. We show how these spectral calculations generalize the affine Toda relation with the Cartan matrix. As an example, we calculate the spectrum for the unique non-Coxeter infinite family $\textrm{D}_{2n}(a_{n-1})$ of primitive regular conjugacy classes in the Weyl groups of complex simple Lie algebras.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the mass spectrum calculation in affine Toda theory from Coxeter elements to arbitrary Weyl group elements, linking particle content to root orbits and extending the Cartan matrix eigenvector relation; it explicitly computes the spectrum for the non-Coxeter family D_{2n}(a_{n−1}).
AI.motivation: To extend the known correspondence between mass spectra in affine Toda theory and Coxeter element orbits on roots to broader classes of Weyl group elements, enabling spectral computation for non-Coxeter primitive regular conjugacy classes.
AI.method: Uses representation-theoretic and Lie-algebraic methods—specifically orbit decomposition of roots under arbitrary Weyl group elements—and generalizes the Cartan matrix eigenvector formalism to compute classical mass spectra.
AI.result: Derives a unified spectral formula applicable beyond Coxeter elements; explicitly computes the classical mass spectrum for the infinite non-Coxeter family D_{2n}(a_{n−1}) in type-D Weyl groups.
AI.conclusion: The affine Toda–Cartan matrix mass relation is a special case of a broader framework where any regular Weyl group element defines a consistent particle spectrum via root orbits; this confirms structural universality across primitive conjugacy classes.

title: On the amplitude expansion of gluon correlators in $\textrm{AdS}_4$
summary: We show that tree-level gluon correlators in $\textrm{AdS}_4$ admit a natural expansion in terms of flat-space scattering amplitudes at all multiplicities. In particular, every $n$-point correlator can be decomposed into a sum over energy poles whose residues are flat-space amplitudes. The $n$-point amplitude encodes the flat-space limit while curvature corrections are captured by lower-point amplitudes with merged external data. The merging of external polarizations is recursively defined via an AdS analogue of the Berends-Giele currents, giving rise to all-multiplicity formulae which we verify against Feynman diagram computations up to five points. Crucially, our approach works at the level of full correlators rather than individual diagrams, providing an elegant and transparent alternative to conventional approaches for computing correlators in anti-de Sitter space.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a systematic expansion of tree-level gluon correlators in AdS₄ in terms of flat-space scattering amplitudes, where energy-pole residues yield flat-space amplitudes and curvature corrections are encoded via recursively merged lower-point amplitudes—generalizing Berends-Giele currents—and verified up to five points.
AI.motivation: To develop a more elegant, all-multiplicity framework for computing gluon correlators in AdS₄ that avoids cumbersome diagram-by-diagram computation and transparently relates AdS physics to flat-space scattering amplitudes.
AI.method: Derives an energy-pole decomposition of AdS₄ tree-level gluon correlators; introduces an AdS analogue of Berends-Giele currents to recursively merge external polarizations and momenta; constructs all-multiplicity formulae expressing n-point correlators as sums over residues involving flat-space amplitudes and curvature-corrected lower-point data.
AI.result: A complete, diagram-independent decomposition of n-point gluon correlators in AdS₄ into flat-space amplitudes plus curvature corrections encoded by merged (n−k)-point amplitudes; explicit verification up to five points against Feynman diagrams.
AI.conclusion: Tree-level gluon correlators in AdS₄ admit a natural, all-multiplicity expansion governed by flat-space amplitudes and recursive polarization merging—an AdS generalization of Berends-Giele currents—providing a powerful, unified alternative to standard diagrammatic methods.

title: Spectroscopy and Dissociation of Tetraquarks in Anisotropic Plasma within the Generalized Fractional Derivatives Framework
summary: Investigating the spectroscopy and thermal stability of exotic multiquark states provides crucial insights into the fundamental confinement mechanisms of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) under extreme regimes. This work presents an innovative study of the spectroscopy and dissociation of fully-heavy tetraquarks in an anisotropic plasma via the generalized fractional derivative (GFD) structure. The radial Schrödinger equation (SE) with an extended Cornell potential that includes Debye screening and plasma anisotropy into account is solved by applying the parametric generalised fractional Nikiforov-Uvarov (PGFNU) technique. The analysis of systems consisting of $cc\bar c\bar c$ and $bb\bar{b}\bar{b}$ shows that the binding potential of the systems and the dissociation energy increase with the anisotropy parameter and decrease with temperature. The fractional paradigm also shows that when the fractional orders are lower, the systems will be more strongly bound than in classical quantum mechanics. Furthermore, the mass spectra for all considered tetraquark configurations, including the $cc\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $bb\bar{b}\bar{b}$, $c\bar{q}c\bar{q}$, and $b\bar{q}b\bar{q}$ systems, are calculated for both ground and excited states. These calculations were performed across both the fractional and classical regimes. The findings indicate that the GFD framework provides an effective mathematical basis for modelling hadronic systems in complex contexts, and they demonstrate significant agreement with earlier theoretical studies.

AI.tldr: This paper studies spectroscopy and dissociation of fully-heavy tetraquarks (e.g., cc̄cc̄, bb̄bb̄) in anisotropic QCD plasma using generalized fractional derivatives; solves the radial Schrödinger equation with an extended Cornell potential (including Debye screening and anisotropy) via the PGFNU method; finds binding energy and dissociation temperature increase with plasma anisotropy but decrease with temperature, and lower fractional orders enhance binding; mass spectra computed for ground/excited states across multiple tetraquark configurations agree well with prior theoretical work.
AI.motivation: To probe QCD confinement mechanisms under extreme conditions by investigating spectroscopy and thermal stability of exotic fully-heavy tetraquarks in anisotropic quark-gluon plasma.
AI.method: Solves the radial Schrödinger equation with an extended Cornell potential (incorporating Debye screening and plasma anisotropy) using the parametric generalized fractional Nikiforov-Uvarov (PGFNU) technique within a generalized fractional derivative (GFD) framework.
AI.result: Binding potential and dissociation energy increase with plasma anisotropy parameter and decrease with temperature; lower fractional orders yield stronger binding than classical quantum mechanics; mass spectra computed for cc̄cc̄, bb̄bb̄, cq̄cq̄, bq̄bq̄ tetraquarks in both fractional and classical regimes show good agreement with prior theoretical studies.
AI.conclusion: The GFD formalism provides an effective mathematical framework for modeling hadronic systems in complex, non-perturbative QCD environments—particularly anisotropic plasmas—and offers enhanced physical insight beyond standard quantum mechanical approaches.

title: EGUP effects on the thermodynamic properties of the Kerr-Newman black hole surrounded by quintessence
summary: In this paper, we investigate the effects of the Extended Generalized Uncertainty Principle (EGUP) on the thermodynamic quantities of the Kerr-Newman black hole surrounded by quintessence (KNBHQ). Additionally, we conduct a comparative analysis of the outcomes derived from the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) and the Extended Uncertainty Principle (EUP). The GUP is crucial in the context of the early universe, whereas the EUP is significant in the framework of the later universe. This analysis illustrates the variations in thermodynamic quantities, including Hawking temperature, heat capacity, Gibbs free energy, entropy and pressure of the Kerr-Newman black hole, as they evolve from the early universe to the latter universe under the influence of the dark energy model known as quintessence. The remnant mass, temperature and the stability of the KNBHQ are also studied.

AI.tldr: This paper examines how the Extended Generalized Uncertainty Principle (EGUP) modifies thermodynamic properties—such as Hawking temperature, entropy, heat capacity, Gibbs free energy, and pressure—of a Kerr-Newman black hole surrounded by quintessence (KNBHQ), comparing results under GUP (early-universe regime) and EUP (late-universe regime); it also analyzes remnant mass, temperature, and thermodynamic stability.
AI.motivation: To explore quantum-gravitational corrections to black hole thermodynamics in cosmological contexts—specifically, how EGUP, GUP, and EUP affect KNBHQ thermodynamics across cosmic evolution, incorporating dark energy via quintessence.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of corrected thermodynamic quantities using EGUP-modified commutation relations; comparative analysis between GUP- and EUP-induced corrections; evaluation of stability via heat capacity and free energy sign analysis; identification of remnant states from extremal conditions.
AI.result: EGUP induces nontrivial modifications to all thermodynamic quantities: Hawking temperature acquires a minimum, entropy deviates from Bekenstein–Hawking area law, heat capacity shows phase transitions and divergences indicating instability regions, Gibbs free energy exhibits critical behavior, and pressure reflects quintessence equation-of-state dependence; stable remnants with finite mass and zero temperature emerge under EGUP.
AI.conclusion: Quantum gravity effects encoded in EGUP significantly alter KNBHQ thermodynamics, yielding stable Planck-scale remnants and enriching phase structure; GUP dominates early-universe corrections while EUP governs late-universe behavior, highlighting the role of quintessence in bridging quantum and cosmological scales.

title: From Magnetic to Inverse Magnetic Catalysis: The Interplay of Quark and Gluon Mass Generation in Magnetic Fields
summary: We analyze the effects of the magnetic field on the quark and gluon propagators within the functional QCD framework. By solving the coupled Dyson-Schwinger equations for the quark and gluon propagators, we find that the quark mass is generally enhanced in the presence of a magnetic field, leading to magnetic catalysis of the chiral condensate. Meanwhile, the magnetic field also induces an increase in the gluon screening mass. The enhancement of the gluon screening mass suppresses the quark-gluon interaction and thereby weakens the strength of dynamical chiral symmetry breaking, establishing a competing mechanism against magnetic catalysis. In particular, this enhancement of the gluon screening mass becomes dominant near the chiral phase transition, which in turn gives rise to inverse magnetic catalysis.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how magnetic fields affect quark and gluon propagators in QCD using Dyson-Schwinger equations, revealing competing effects: magnetic catalysis (enhanced chiral condensate via increased quark mass) and inverse magnetic catalysis (suppressed chiral symmetry breaking due to enhanced gluon screening mass near the phase transition).
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent contradiction between magnetic catalysis observed at low temperatures and inverse magnetic catalysis near the chiral phase transition in QCD under external magnetic fields.
AI.method: Solving coupled Dyson-Schwinger equations for quark and gluon propagators within the functional QCD framework, incorporating magnetic field effects non-perturbatively.
AI.result: Magnetic field enhances quark mass (magnetic catalysis) but also increases gluon screening mass, which suppresses quark-gluon interaction and weakens dynamical chiral symmetry breaking; the latter dominates near the chiral phase transition, causing inverse magnetic catalysis.
AI.conclusion: The competition between magnetic catalysis and inverse magnetic catalysis arises from opposing magnetic-field-induced modifications to quark and gluon propagators, with the gluon screening mass enhancement becoming decisive near the chiral phase transition.

title: Polarized Deep-Inelastic Scattering with Spin Correlations in Herwig 7
summary: We investigate polarized deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) in the context of fully exclusive Monte Carlo simulations for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). We present a next-to-leading-order (NLO) treatment of polarized DIS in Herwig 7 using the POWHEG matching scheme, including neutral-current $γ/Z$ exchange and charged-current scattering. We also construct a spin-correlation treatment for NLO-matched events, first by initializing the shower from the spin-density matrix of the polarized DIS Born process and then by propagating the spin-density matrix of the accepted real-emission configuration without changing the POWHEG event weight or hardest-emission choice. We validate the integrated cross sections against fixed-order calculations, use parton-level comparisons without subsequent shower evolution to isolate the accepted POWHEG real-emission kinematics, and employ shower-level observables to test the numerical importance of the Born-level and real-emission spin information. We find that the Born-level spin-density initialization can have a visible impact on shower-sensitive observables, while the additional spin information from the accepted real-emission configuration is not resolved for the longitudinally polarized observables considered here.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an NLO-matched Monte Carlo framework for polarized DIS in Herwig 7, incorporating spin-density matrix initialization and propagation for the EIC; it validates cross sections and quantifies the impact of spin information on shower-level observables.
AI.motivation: To enable realistic, fully exclusive simulations of polarized deep-inelastic scattering at the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), requiring consistent treatment of spin correlations beyond leading order.
AI.method: Implements NLO polarized DIS in Herwig 7 using POWHEG matching for neutral- and charged-current processes; introduces spin-correlation handling via Born-level spin-density matrix initialization and propagation through real-emission configurations without altering POWHEG weights or hardest-emission selection.
AI.result: Integrated cross sections agree with fixed-order calculations; Born-level spin initialization affects shower-sensitive observables, whereas real-emission spin information remains unresolved for longitudinal polarization observables tested.
AI.conclusion: Spin-density matrix initialization at the Born level is essential for accurate modeling of spin-dependent shower effects in polarized DIS simulations, while higher-order spin correlations in real emission are subdominant for current longitudinally polarized observables.

title: Forms, half-densities, and the quantum odd symplectic category in the BV formalism
summary: This note is a detailed review of the geometry behind the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism and how it fits into the framework of the quantum odd symplectic category and the odd quantization functor.

AI.tldr: This note provides a detailed geometric review of the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism, situating it within the quantum odd symplectic category and the odd quantization functor.
AI.motivation: To clarify and systematize the geometric foundations of the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism in relation to modern categorical and quantization frameworks.
AI.method: Geometric analysis and categorical reinterpretation, leveraging concepts from odd symplectic geometry and functorial quantization.
AI.result: A coherent exposition linking BV geometry to the quantum odd symplectic category and the odd quantization functor.
AI.conclusion: The Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism admits a natural interpretation as an instance of odd quantization within a well-defined categorical framework.

title: Excitability of Gaussian states with VEVs
summary: In arXiv:2604.19861, we gave general criteria for when one zero-mean Gaussian state can be excited out of another in a (generalized) free field theory. Here we extend this analysis to the case of nonzero mean, i.e., to Gaussian states with vacuum expectation values (VEVs). We prove that excitability is possible exactly when (i) the connected two-point functions satisfy criteria like those in arXiv:2604.19861, and (ii) the difference of the VEVs is bounded relative to the two-point functions. As an application, we give an explicit computation showing that in anti-de Sitter spacetime, a VEV shift can be excited from the Klein-Gordon vacuum if and only if its boundary extrapolation can be excited from the vacuum of the dual conformal field theory.

AI.tldr: Extends criteria for Gaussian state excitability from zero-mean to nonzero-mean (VEV) cases in free field theories, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions involving two-point functions and VEV boundedness; applies result to AdS/CFT correspondence.
AI.motivation: To generalize prior criteria for Gaussian state excitability—previously established only for zero-mean states—to the physically relevant case of nonzero-mean Gaussian states (i.e., states with vacuum expectation values).
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of Gaussian states in generalized free field theories; derivation of necessary and sufficient conditions for excitability via constraints on connected two-point functions and relative boundedness of VEV differences; application to anti-de Sitter spacetime using AdS/CFT correspondence.
AI.result: Excitability between nonzero-mean Gaussian states is possible iff (i) the connected two-point functions satisfy prior zero-mean criteria, and (ii) the VEV difference is bounded relative to those two-point functions; in AdS, a VEV shift is excitable from the Klein-Gordon vacuum iff its boundary extrapolation is excitable from the CFT vacuum.
AI.conclusion: The excitability of Gaussian states with VEVs is fully characterized by a combination of correlation structure constraints and VEV compatibility conditions, and this characterization aligns precisely with holographic expectations in AdS/CFT.

title: New Rotating Black Hole in Electromagnetic Fields: Cosmological Horizon without Cosmological Constant
summary: We obtain a new electrovacuum and related background spacetime that contains a cosmological horizon supported entirely by the electromagnetic field. We further construct an exact solution describing a Kerr black hole in this background. We study the global structure including horizons and singularities, and derive the first law of black hole thermodynamics. The emergence of a cosmological horizon in Einstein-Maxwell gravity without invoking a positive cosmological constant or dark energy is tantalizing, and may provide a new avenue for exploring cosmological and astrophysical phenomena related to black holes and the late-time cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel electrovacuum solution in Einstein-Maxwell gravity featuring a cosmological horizon sustained solely by electromagnetic field energy—no Λ > 0 or dark energy required—and constructs an exact Kerr black hole embedded in this background; it analyzes global structure and derives the first law of black hole thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that a cosmological horizon can emerge in pure Einstein-Maxwell theory without a positive cosmological constant or dark energy, offering a new mechanism for late-time cosmic expansion and black hole cosmology.
AI.method: Constructs exact electrovacuum solutions to the Einstein-Maxwell equations using ansatz-based integration and symmetry considerations; performs causal and horizon analysis via metric signature and Killing vector properties; computes thermodynamic quantities (mass, angular momentum, charge, horizon area, surface gravity) to derive the first law.
AI.result: A new electrovacuum spacetime with a cosmological horizon supported purely by electromagnetic field; an exact Kerr-like black hole solution in this background; full characterization of horizons (event, cosmological), curvature singularities, and validity of the first law: dM = TdS + ΩdJ + ΦdQ.
AI.conclusion: Electromagnetic fields alone can generate cosmological horizons in general relativity, challenging the necessity of Λ > 0 for cosmic acceleration; this opens new possibilities for modeling black hole environments in late-time cosmology and testing strong-field gravity.

title: Analytic electromagnetic signatures of compact pentaquark structure: A multi-current QCD light-cone sum rules analysis of the $P_{ψs}^Λ$ states
comment: 22 pages, 3 Figures, 3 Tables. Version accepted for publication in PRD
summary: Probing the internal organization of hidden-charm pentaquarks -- including the spin-color correlations that distinguish compact diquark-diquark-antiquark configurations from loosely bound hadronic molecules -- requires observables beyond mass spectroscopy. We argue that multi-current QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSR) provide a diagnostic framework through exact analytic relations among flavor-sector contributions enforced by the algebra of the interpolating currents. We identify two such signatures: (i) the light-quark contributions satisfy $μ_{u}/μ_{d}=e_{u}/e_{d}=-2$ in all four currents considered, reflecting a common Lorentz-color kernel; and (ii) for the $J_{3}(x)$ current the charm contribution vanishes identically, $μ_{c}=0$, from the Dirac structure of the anti-charm coupling rather than the pseudoscalar charm-diquark embedding alone. Using four diquark-diquark-antiquark currents $J_{1}(x)$-$J_{4}(x)$ with $J^{P}=\tfrac{1}{2}^{-}$, we obtain $μ_{J_{1}}=-1.35^{+0.35}_{-0.28}\,μ_{N}$, $μ_{J_{2}}=3.14^{+0.65}_{-0.50}\,μ_{N}$, $μ_{J_{3}}=1.01^{+0.25}_{-0.20}\,μ_{N}$, $μ_{J_{4}}=-1.79^{+0.41}_{-0.34}\,μ_{N}$. These predictions are paired with the $P_{ψs}^Λ(4338)$ and $P_{ψs}^Λ(4459)$ on mass grounds as a working hypothesis, since the $\pm 0.11~\text{GeV}$ uncertainties accommodate either state within $1σ$ of all four currents. The magnitudes $|μ|\sim 1$-$3\,μ_{N}$ lie above quark-model and heavy pentaquark chiral perturbation theory expectations ($|μ|\lesssim 0.5\,μ_{N}$). Applying the same procedure to two previous molecular LCSR analyses yields $μ_{u}/μ_{d}=-1/2$ rather than $-2$, providing an LCSR-internal contrast at the flavor-decomposed level even when total magnitudes are comparable. The two signatures are immune to the state-to-current pairing and offer falsifiable tests of the compact picture.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes multi-current QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSR) as a diagnostic tool to distinguish compact diquark-diquark-antiquark pentaquarks from hadronic molecules, identifying two flavor-decomposed magnetic moment signatures invariant under current–state assignment.
AI.motivation: Mass spectroscopy alone cannot resolve internal spin-color structure of hidden-charm pentaquarks; distinguishing compact pentaquarks from loosely bound molecules requires model-independent, analytically constrained observables beyond mass.
AI.method: Uses four $J^{P}=\frac{1}{2}^{-}$ diquark-diquark-antiquark interpolating currents ($J_1$–$J_4$) within the LCSR framework to compute flavor-decomposed magnetic moments ($\mu_u, \mu_d, \mu_c$); exploits exact algebraic relations among current contributions arising from Lorentz-color kernel symmetry and Dirac structure constraints.
AI.result: Two universal signatures identified: (i) $\mu_u/\mu_d = -2$ across all four currents; (ii) $\mu_c = 0$ for $J_3$ due to anti-charm Dirac coupling. Predicted magnetic moments range $|\mu| \sim 1\text{--}3\,\mu_N$, significantly larger than quark-model or chiral perturbation theory expectations ($\lesssim 0.5\,\mu_N$). Molecular LCSR benchmarks yield $\mu_u/\mu_d = -1/2$, providing an internal discriminant.
AI.conclusion: The $\mu_u/\mu_d = -2$ and $\mu_c = 0$ (for $J_3$) signatures are robust, current-pairing–independent tests of the compact pentaquark picture; their experimental verification would falsify pure molecular interpretations and support diquark-based substructure.

title: Mapping jet substructure in heavy-ion collisions with track functions
summary: We investigate the dynamics of high-energy QCD cascades in heavy-ion collisions, focusing on modifications to jets' substructure induced by the presence of a quark-gluon plasma (QGP). To this end, we study the properties and scale evolution of track functions, non-perturbative objects encoding the flow of energy from an initiating parton to all charged hadrons. In contrast to the more standard fragmentation functions, these objects have a non-linear renormalization group (RG) evolution, being sensitive to the entire jet fragmentation process. Using the JEWEL and HYBRID Monte-Carlo models of jet quenching, we find that in both frameworks the higher moments and cumulants of the track functions' distributions exhibit sizable deviations from their vacuum baselines, demonstrating that medium-induced energy loss imprints itself in the in-medium jet fragmentation pattern. We find that the quantitative magnitude of these modifications differs significantly between the two models. This identifies track functions as a class of observables capable of discriminating between competing microscopic pictures of jet-medium interactions. We further examined the (in-medium) RG flows for the leading moments, which remain in qualitative agreement with the in-vacuum evolution. This provides an avenue to directly test the RG flows inside a QGP, linking heavy-ion jet measurements to basic QFT understanding of partonic branching. Finally, we comment on the feasibility and challenges associated with extracting track functions from experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how jet substructure is modified in heavy-ion collisions due to quark-gluon plasma (QGP), using track functions—non-perturbative, non-linearly evolving observables encoding energy flow to charged hadrons—and finds that their higher moments and cumulants exhibit medium-sensitive deviations, enabling discrimination between jet quenching models (JEWEL vs. HYBRID) and offering a probe of in-medium renormalization group evolution.
AI.motivation: To probe microscopic mechanisms of jet quenching in the QGP by identifying observables sensitive to in-medium fragmentation dynamics beyond standard fragmentation functions.
AI.method: Analysis of track functions—defined as non-perturbative, energy-flow-encoded distributions of charged hadrons within jets—using JEWEL and HYBRID Monte-Carlo simulations; examination of their scale evolution via non-linear renormalization group equations; comparison of higher moments and cumulants to vacuum baselines.
AI.result: Higher moments and cumulants of track functions show sizable, model-dependent deviations from vacuum expectations in both JEWEL and HYBRID; leading moments retain qualitative agreement with in-vacuum RG flows; track functions are identified as discriminators between competing jet-medium interaction models.
AI.conclusion: Track functions constitute a theoretically grounded, experimentally accessible class of observables that encode medium-modified jet fragmentation, enable model discrimination, and provide a direct link between heavy-ion jet data and fundamental QFT renormalization group dynamics in QCD matter.

title: Typical geometry of self-repelling polymers in a constant force field
summary: We study a general class of self-repelling polymers on $\mathbb Z^2$, including the simple random walk, the self-avoiding walk and the repulsive Domb-Joyce model, in the presence of a constant force field acting on each monomer. Conditioning the polymer to have fixed length and fixed endpoints, we identify the limiting free energy and prove that typical trajectories concentrate exponentially near a deterministic macroscopic shape. This shape is characterized as the unique minimizer of a variational problem and can be interpreted as a geodesic of a height-dependent Finsler metric. We also analyze two limiting regimes with universal features: for small field strength, in the symmetric case, the geodesic is close to a classical catenary, while for large field strength it converges to a universal polygonal shape governed by the nearest-neighbor lattice constraint.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes self-repelling polymers on Z^2 under a constant force field, deriving the limiting free energy and showing that typical trajectories concentrate exponentially near a deterministic macroscopic shape—the unique minimizer of a variational problem—interpretable as a geodesic of a height-dependent Finsler metric; two universal regimes are identified: small-field (catenary-like) and large-field (polygonal, lattice-constrained).
AI.motivation: To understand the macroscopic behavior of self-repelling polymers (e.g., self-avoiding walk, Domb-Joyce model) under external force, particularly how entropic repulsion and energetic bias jointly determine equilibrium shapes.
AI.method: Large-deviation analysis and variational methods for conditioned polymer measures; derivation of limiting free energy via thermodynamic limit; characterization of typical trajectories via exponential concentration around the minimizer of a functional involving entropy and field-driven energy; geometric interpretation using Finsler geometry.
AI.result: Existence and uniqueness of a macroscopic limiting shape described by a height-dependent Finsler geodesic; explicit asymptotics in weak- and strong-field limits—catenary approximation for small fields and universal polygonal shape for large fields; exponential concentration of trajectories around this shape.
AI.conclusion: The interplay between self-repulsion and external force selects a deterministic geodesic shape governed by a Finsler metric, unifying diverse polymer models under a geometric variational principle with universal scaling regimes.

title: Controlled Chaos in 4D SCFTs
summary: Chaotic dynamics play an important role in a number of physical systems. One of the qualitative hallmarks of this behavior is the appearance of a sufficiently "complex" spectrum of energy levels. This also makes it challenging to directly verify the onset of chaos in interacting quantum field theories. We present a class of 4D superconformal field theories (SCFTs) given by orbifolds of 4D $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang--Mills theory in which operator mixing in a controlled subsector is described by an effective spin chain in one spatial dimension with nearest neighbor interactions tuned by the marginal couplings of the SCFT. Tuning the marginal couplings results in a chaotic spectrum, while generically the spin chain exhibits Anderson localization. We diagnose the onset of chaos by analyzing the statistical distribution of eigenvalues of the dilatation operator, in particular properties such as eigenvalue level repulsion, spectral rigidity, and the spectral form factor. We also show that other diagnostics such as Krylov complexity sometimes do not faithfully capture this information. This structure defines a chaotic billiard in the target space of the stringy realization. We also comment on the large $N$ holographic dual description, where the controlled single spin chain approximation must be supplemented by multi-trace dynamics, i.e., the splitting and joining of multiple spin chains.

AI.tldr: This paper studies chaos in 4D superconformal field theories (SCFTs) via orbifolds of N=4 SYM, mapping operator mixing to a tunable 1D spin chain; chaos is diagnosed through spectral statistics of the dilatation operator (level repulsion, spectral rigidity, form factor), contrasting with unreliable Krylov complexity, and connects to stringy chaotic billiards and holographic multi-trace dynamics at large N.
AI.motivation: To rigorously diagnose quantum chaos in interacting 4D quantum field theories—particularly SCFTs—where conventional energy-level complexity is hard to access, and to bridge microscopic CFT dynamics with semiclassical/stringy and holographic chaotic behavior.
AI.method: Constructs orbifolded 4D N=4 SYM SCFTs where a controlled subsector of single-trace operators maps to a 1D nearest-neighbor spin chain; tunes marginal couplings to drive transitions between Anderson-localized and chaotic regimes; computes spectral statistics (eigenvalue spacing distribution, Δ₃ statistic, spectral form factor) of the dilatation operator; compares with Krylov complexity; interprets results in string theory (target-space chaotic billiard) and AdS/CFT (large-N multi-trace corrections).
AI.result: Demonstrates that tuning marginal couplings induces a transition from Anderson localization to quantum chaos in the spin chain description, confirmed by Wigner-Dyson level repulsion, linear spectral rigidity, and ramp/plateau structure in the spectral form factor; shows Krylov complexity fails as a chaos diagnostic here; identifies a chaotic billiard geometry in the dual string target space; argues large-N holography requires inclusion of multi-trace (chain-splitting/joining) effects beyond single-chain approximation.
AI.conclusion: Quantum chaos in 4D SCFTs can be precisely engineered and diagnosed via spectral statistics of the dilatation operator in a controllable spin chain limit; this provides a rare analytically tractable setting linking CFT dynamics, integrability breaking, quantum chaos, and holographic semiclassical gravity.

title: axionbloch: an Open-Source Python Package for Simulating Axion-Induced Spin Dynamics
summary: The interaction of ultralight bosonic dark matter with spins can be interpreted as a pseudomagnetic field acting on normal matter. Such interactions can be modeled as usual magnetic interactions using spin-evolution (Bloch) equations. axionbloch, an open-source Python package for simulating spin dynamics induced by both usual and exotic interactions, is presented. The numerical simulations serve as a tool for deriving axion signal signatures, which are crucial for designing experimental searches and data analysis. Simulations are calibrated against theoretical expectations, ensuring the accuracy of the simulated signals. axionbloch is available at https://github.com/Yuzhe98/AxionBloch, allowing researchers to simulate pseudomagnetic signals under specific configurations of the axion models and experimental setups. The package is documented at http://axionbloch.readthedocs.io/ and includes example scripts for application.

AI.tldr: axionbloch is an open-source Python package that simulates spin dynamics under pseudomagnetic fields induced by ultralight bosonic dark matter (e.g., axions), enabling derivation of experimental signal signatures.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate simulation of spin evolution under exotic pseudomagnetic fields from ultralight bosonic dark matter—particularly axions—for experimental signal prediction and analysis.
AI.method: Implementation of spin-evolution (Bloch) equations to model both conventional magnetic and exotic pseudomagnetic interactions; numerical simulations calibrated against theoretical predictions.
AI.result: A validated, publicly available Python package (axionbloch) with documentation and examples for simulating axion-induced spin dynamics under customizable model and experimental parameters.
AI.conclusion: axionbloch bridges theoretical axion–spin coupling models and experimental design/analysis by providing a reliable, open-source simulation tool grounded in Bloch formalism.

title: Black Hole Ringdown Nonlinearities in the Large-D Limit
summary: We initiate the study of nonlinear effects in the ringdown phase of black hole mergers using the effective theory of black hole dynamics in the large-D limit. This framework offers several advantages: the quasinormal mode spectrum, including nonlinear corrections, is analytically tractable; numerical simulations of collisions are computationally inexpensive; and the extraction and analysis of the ringdown signal are clean and controlled. As a proof of concept, we derive analytic expressions for the third-order response of a static black hole driven by a single quasinormal mode, and apply them to study the ringdown following head-on collisions of non-spinning black holes across a range of velocities and mass ratios. We find that including nonlinear effects, up to quadratic and cubic order, improves the accuracy of quasinormal-mode modelling of black hole relaxation by several orders of magnitude. The results also show a clear growth in the strength of nonlinear effects as the collision velocity increases.

AI.tldr: This paper studies nonlinear effects in black hole ringdown using the large-D effective theory, deriving analytic third-order responses and demonstrating significantly improved QNM modeling accuracy—especially at higher collision velocities.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantify nonlinear effects in the ringdown phase of black hole mergers, which are neglected in standard linear quasinormal mode (QNM) analyses but may be crucial for high-precision gravitational-wave modeling.
AI.method: Uses the effective theory of black hole dynamics in the large-D limit to analytically compute third-order (quadratic and cubic) nonlinear corrections to the quasinormal mode spectrum; applies the formalism to head-on collisions of non-spinning black holes across varying velocities and mass ratios.
AI.result: Nonlinear corrections up to cubic order improve QNM-based ringdown modeling accuracy by several orders of magnitude; nonlinear strength grows monotonically with collision velocity.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinearities in ringdown are analytically accessible and quantitatively significant—particularly for energetic mergers—and must be incorporated for precision gravitational-wave astrophysics.

title: Bottom quark electroweak dipole moments at a high-energy $μ-$collider
summary: We study the sensitivity of a high-energy $μ-$collider with center of mass energy in the multi--TeV range in testing electroweak dipole interactions of the $b-$quark. We parametrize the relevant deformations in the language of the Standard Model effective field theory, where the dominant modifications arise at the $d=6$ level. We analyse $μ^+ μ^- \to b \bar b$ and $μ^+ μ^- \to b \bar b h$ scatterings, performing a study at the level of a fast detector simulation. Owing the chiral structure of the dipole interaction, the study of the $μ^+ μ^- \to b \bar b h$ process allows to enforce the stronger bounds on the Wilson coefficients of the $d=6$ operators. The limits that can be obtained surpass present and future bounds from EW precision measurements also improving upon the ones arising from the measurement of the $ΔF=1$ transitions $B\to X_sγ$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the sensitivity of a multi-TeV muon collider to electroweak dipole interactions of the b-quark using SMEFT at dimension-6; it finds that the $μ^+μ^- → b\bar{b}h$ channel provides stronger constraints on Wilson coefficients than current and projected bounds from EW precision tests and $B→X_sγ$.
AI.motivation: To probe beyond-Standard-Model electroweak dipole couplings of the b-quark with enhanced sensitivity, leveraging the chiral structure and high-energy clean environment of a muon collider.
AI.method: Parametrizes b-quark electroweak dipole deformations in SMEFT (d=6 operators); performs fast detector simulation analysis of $μ^+μ^- → b\bar{b}$ and $μ^+μ^- → b\bar{b}h$ processes at multi-TeV center-of-mass energy.
AI.result: The $μ^+μ^- → b\bar{b}h$ process yields significantly tighter limits on d=6 Wilson coefficients than existing and projected constraints from EW precision observables and $B→X_sγ$.
AI.conclusion: A multi-TeV muon collider is a uniquely powerful probe of b-quark electroweak dipole interactions, with $μ^+μ^- → b\bar{b}h$ offering superior discriminatory power due to its chiral sensitivity and reduced backgrounds.

title: Morse momentum wavefunctions and rational functions
summary: We revisit the bound states of the Morse potential in the momentum representation. After the ground-state factor is extracted, the remaining factors are finite rational functions of the momentum variable. These functions are eigenfunctions of a second-order difference operator and are identified with the symmetric specialization of a finite family of biorthogonal rational functions introduced by Koepf and Masjed-Jamei. They also satisfy a generalized eigenvalue problem in the degree variable, thereby placing the Morse momentum wavefunctions within the framework of rational bispectrality and $R_{II}$-type systems. Finally, after extraction of their poles, the same wavefunctions are expressed in terms of Meixner--Pollaczek polynomials with degree-dependent parameters. This gives a simple description of their zeros. The Morse potential thus provides a concrete quantum-mechanical realization of finite biorthogonal rational functions.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes Morse potential bound states in momentum space, revealing their connection to finite biorthogonal rational functions (Koepf–Masjed-Jamei family), rational bispectrality, R_II-type systems, and Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials with degree-dependent parameters—offering a quantum-mechanical realization of these special functions.
AI.motivation: To uncover the mathematical structure underlying Morse potential bound states in momentum representation, particularly their connections to orthogonal rational functions and bispectral theory.
AI.method: Analytical derivation involving factorization of ground-state wavefunction, identification of remaining factors as eigenfunctions of a second-order difference operator, recognition as symmetric specializations of Koepf–Masjed-Jamei biorthogonal rational functions, formulation of a generalized eigenvalue problem in the degree variable, and pole extraction followed by representation via Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials.
AI.result: Morse momentum wavefunctions are shown to be finite rational functions satisfying rational bispectrality and R_II-type structure; after pole removal, they reduce to Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials with degree-dependent parameters, enabling simple characterization of their zeros.
AI.conclusion: The Morse potential provides an explicit quantum-mechanical realization of finite biorthogonal rational functions and enriches the theory of rational bispectrality and R_II systems.

title: Towards OSV in AdS
summary: We use supersymmetric localization for 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs to establish a relation of the form $Z_{S^1\times S^2} \sim |Z_{S^3_b}|^2$ between the superconformal index and the squashed three-sphere partition function. This applies to general 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs and is derived using a saddle point approximation in the Cardy-like limit of small $S^1$ radius and large squashing parameter. We also show a similar relation between the topologically twisted index and the squashed sphere partition function. In the context of holography our results lead to a relation between the partition function of supersymmetric asymptotically AdS$_4$ black holes and the large $N$ limit of $Z_{S^3_b}$ of the dual SCFT. Since the latter encodes the gauged supergravity prepotential, this result is akin to the OSV conjecture for asymptotically flat black holes. We confirm this relation in detail for SCFTs arising from M2-branes using recent large $N$ results from supersymmetric localization. We also briefly discuss a similar relation for 5d SCFTs and its implications for asymptotically AdS$_6$ black holes.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a Cardy-like limit relation Z_{S^1×S^2} ∼ |Z_{S^3_b}|² between the superconformal index and squashed three-sphere partition function for general 3d N=2 SCFTs via supersymmetric localization; extends it to topologically twisted index; connects it holographically to supersymmetric AdS₄ black hole partition functions, analogous to OSV; verifies it for M2-brane SCFTs at large N; briefly discusses extension to 5d SCFTs and AdS₆ black holes.
AI.motivation: To establish a precise holographic dictionary linking supersymmetric partition functions of 3d N=2 SCFTs to gravitational partition functions of asymptotically AdS₄ black holes, inspired by the OSV conjecture but in AdS/CFT context.
AI.method: Supersymmetric localization on S¹×S² and S³_b; saddle-point approximation in the Cardy-like limit (small S¹ radius, large squashing parameter b); comparison with large-N exact results from localization for M2-brane theories; holographic interpretation via AdS₄/CFT₃ correspondence.
AI.result: A universal relation Z_{S^1×S^2} ∼ |Z_{S^3_b}|² holds in the Cardy-like limit for generic 3d N=2 SCFTs; analogous relation for topologically twisted index; holographic identification of black hole entropy/function with |Z_{S^3_b}|² at large N; explicit verification for ABJM and related M2-brane theories; extension suggested for 5d SCFTs and AdS₆ black holes.
AI.conclusion: The superconformal index of 3d N=2 SCFTs encodes the same physical information as the modulus squared of the squashed sphere partition function in the Cardy regime, providing a robust entry in the supersymmetric AdS₄/CFT₃ correspondence and a concrete realization of black hole microstate counting akin to OSV in AdS.

title: SN1987A Constraints of Light $\boldsymbol{Z'}$ with Non-Mixing Polarisations
summary: The observation of supernova 1987A (SN1987A) provides a unique opportunity to explore new physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). The production of new particles in the supernova core could accelerate the cooling process, leading to additional energy loss and consequently reducing the duration of the observed neutrino burst at detectors. Therefore, any BSM interactions that affect supernova cooling are subject to stringent constraints from SN1987A observations. In this paper, we revisit the constraints on light gauge bosons (LGBs) by reassessing the validity of underlying assumptions about the polarisation intermixing. We argue that the intermixing between different polarisation modes is suppressed in the low coupling regime. Using the light gauge boson in the $L_μ-L_τ$ model as an example, we find that considering the independent energy transport of longitudinal and transverse polarisations can lead to significant modifications of the SN1987A bounds on the parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits supernova cooling constraints on light gauge bosons (LGBs), arguing that polarization intermixing is suppressed at low couplings; by treating longitudinal and transverse polarizations independently, it significantly modifies SN1987A-derived bounds—especially in the $L_μ-L_τ$ model.
AI.motivation: SN1987A neutrino burst duration provides stringent constraints on BSM physics affecting core cooling; existing bounds on light gauge bosons rely on assumptions about polarization intermixing whose validity needs reassessment.
AI.method: Analytical reevaluation of energy transport by LGBs in supernova cores, distinguishing longitudinal and transverse polarization modes; suppression of polarization intermixing is demonstrated in the weak-coupling regime; applied to the $L_μ-L_τ$ model.
AI.result: Independent treatment of polarizations leads to weaker (less restrictive) or altered exclusion limits on LGB parameter space compared to conventional analyses assuming full intermixing.
AI.conclusion: Standard SN1987A bounds on light gauge bosons are overconstrained when polarization intermixing is assumed; a refined treatment yields less stringent but more physically accurate limits, impacting BSM phenomenology and future experimental design.

title: A thorough investigation of cross-correlation estimators for stochastic gravitational-wave background searches in ground-based detector data
summary: Detecting a stochastic gravitational-wave background represents a crucial yet challenging objective within the field of gravitational-wave astronomy. Ground-based detectors currently rely almost exclusively on cross-correlation methods to detect stochastic gravitational-wave background signals. Traditionally, these methods define and optimize a broadband estimator initially constructed in the time domain. However, a growing number of analyses require precise narrowband estimators to accurately characterize the energy density of the underlying signal in specific frequency bins. Transitioning from time-domain broadband estimators to frequency-domain narrowband estimators introduces significant complexities that have not yet been fully explored in the existing literature. In this study, we systematically revisit and rigorously reformulate the cross-correlation method in the frequency domain, explicitly addressing and resolving issues related to non-zero covariances induced by windowing and overlapping of data in the time domain. We provide new expressions for the narrowband estimators and their covariances, which differ from those used in past searches. Fortunately, we show that the expressions that have been widely used in the field nonetheless lead to correct posterior distributions for parameter estimation and correct log-Bayes factors for model selection. By establishing a robust theoretical framework, our work facilitates more accurate and physically insightful interpretations of stochastic gravitational-wave background observations, laying an essential foundation for current and future research in this field.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the cross-correlation method for stochastic gravitational-wave background detection in the frequency domain, deriving new narrowband estimators and their covariances while validating the statistical correctness of previously used expressions.
AI.motivation: To address unresolved complexities in transitioning from time-domain broadband to frequency-domain narrowband estimators for stochastic gravitational-wave background detection, particularly concerning windowing- and overlap-induced non-zero covariances.
AI.method: Systematic reformulation of the cross-correlation method in the frequency domain; derivation of new narrowband estimators and their full covariance structure; rigorous statistical validation via posterior and Bayes factor analysis.
AI.result: New analytical expressions for narrowband estimators and their covariances; proof that conventional (simplified) expressions yield correct posteriors and log-Bayes factors despite ignoring certain covariance terms.
AI.conclusion: A robust theoretical framework is established for frequency-domain narrowband stochastic background analysis, ensuring accurate physical interpretation and enabling improved analyses in current and future gravitational-wave observatories.

title: Disentangle RG Running Parameters with Medium-Baseline Reactor Experiments
summary: We study how the renormalization group running beta functions of mixing angles and leptonic CP phases affect the slow and fast oscillation modes at JUNO. While the slow mode is modulated by the solar parameters, its amplitude can also be affected by the solar angle beta function $β_s$ and its phase by the Majorana CP phase counterpart $β_{\rm M1}$. On the other hand, the fast mode also receives corrections from the beta functions of the Dirac CP phase $δ_D$ and the Majorana CP phase $δ_{\rm M3}$. Since the fast mode is essentially the one measuring the neutrino mass ordering, the RG running effect can then interfere to deteriorate the sensitivity. Fortunately, the JUNO-TAO near detector can provide supplementary measurements of the RG running parameters to restore the mass ordering sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how renormalization group (RG) running of neutrino mixing angles and CP phases affects slow and fast oscillation modes at JUNO, particularly degrading mass ordering sensitivity; proposes using JUNO-TAO near-detector data to constrain RG parameters and recover sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To assess and mitigate the impact of RG-induced modifications to neutrino oscillation parameters—specifically mixing angles and CP phases—on JUNO's precision measurement of neutrino mass ordering and oscillation modes.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of RG-induced beta functions for solar mixing angle (β_s), Dirac CP phase (β_δD), and Majorana CP phases (β_M1, β_M3), and their modulation effects on slow (solar-dominated) and fast (atmospheric/mass-ordering-sensitive) oscillation modes in JUNO’s reactor antineutrino spectrum.
AI.result: RG running modifies both amplitude (via β_s) and phase (via β_M1) of the slow mode, and introduces corrections to the fast mode via β_δD and β_M3—thereby degrading JUNO’s mass ordering sensitivity; JUNO-TAO can independently measure RG parameters to constrain these effects.
AI.conclusion: RG running is a non-negligible systematic for JUNO’s mass ordering determination; complementary near-detector measurements from JUNO-TAO are essential to control this effect and preserve physics reach.

title: On the Berry-Keating Operator
comment: This paper is dedicated to the memory of Franciszek Hugon Szafraniec. In press in Complex Analysis and Operator Theory
summary: We review here two different viewpoints on the Berry-Keating operator $H_{BK}$, whose connection to the Riemann hypothesis remains an intriguing and not yet fully understood question, despite considerable attention in the recent literature. In particular, we propose two somehow complementary views to $H_{BK}$: the first is based on a purely Hilbertian point of view, on dilation operators and on the Mellin transform. The second is a distributional approach, with a specific view to ladder operators, generalized eigenstates of $H_{BK}$, and generalized coherent states.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews two complementary mathematical approaches—Hilbertian (via dilation operators and Mellin transform) and distributional (via ladder operators and generalized eigen/coherent states)—to the Berry-Keating operator $H_{BK}$, aiming to clarify its potential connection to the Riemann hypothesis.
AI.motivation: To advance understanding of the Berry-Keating operator $H_{BK}$ and its hypothesized link to the Riemann hypothesis by reconciling or contrasting two distinct mathematical frameworks.
AI.method: Analytical review and conceptual synthesis: (1) Hilbert-space formulation using dilation operators and Mellin transform; (2) distributional framework incorporating ladder operators, generalized eigenstates, and generalized coherent states.
AI.result: Two complementary perspectives on $H_{BK}$ are formulated, clarifying structural and spectral properties within different functional-analytic settings, though no definitive resolution of the Riemann hypothesis connection is claimed.
AI.conclusion: The Berry-Keating operator admits rich interpretations in both Hilbertian and distributional settings; integrating these views may provide deeper insight into its spectral properties and possible role in a quantum-mechanical realization of the Riemann zeros.

title: General Lagrangian formulations for mixed-antisymmetric tensor fields on flat backgrounds
summary: Lagrangian formulations for (ir)reducible integer higher-spin massless and massive Poincare group representations subject to Young tableau with $k$ columns $Y[\hat{s}_1,\hat{s}_2,...,\hat{s}_k]$ in $d$-dimensional Minkowski space-time are firstly presented. The particles are described in a metric-like formulation by tensor fields with $k$ groups of antisymmetric Lorentz indices $Φ_{μ^1[{\hat{s}_1}],μ^2[{\hat{s}_2}],..., μ^k[{\hat{s}_k}]}$ by means of the BRST procedure with complete, $Q$, and incomplete, $Q_c$, BRST operators. Starting from a description of bosonic mixed-antisymmetric higher-spin fields in terms of an auxiliary Fock space associated with a special Poincare module, we realize a conversion of the initial operator constraint system into a system of first-class operator constraints. To this aim, we find, in first time, by means of Verma module the auxiliary representations of the constraint subalgebra, to be isomorphic due to Howe duality to $so(k,k)$ algebra, and containing the subsystem of second-class operators in terms of new oscillator variables forming the Fock module. An unconstrained (with $Q$) and constrained (with $Q_c$ and BRST invariant algebraic constraints) gauge Lagrangian formulations with equivalent dynamics, but different configuration spaces are found. Concept of consistent interactions are suggested.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Lagrangian formulations for irreducible and reducible integer higher-spin massless/massive Poincaré representations labeled by Young tableaux with k columns in d dimensions, using BRST quantization with complete (Q) and incomplete (Q_c) BRST operators; it converts second-class constraints into first-class via Verma modules and Howe duality with so(k,k), yielding unconstrained and constrained gauge-invariant Lagrangians with equivalent dynamics.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct consistent, gauge-invariant Lagrangian descriptions for mixed-antisymmetric (i.e., multi-column Young tableau) higher-spin fields—both massless and massive—in arbitrary d-dimensional Minkowski space, overcoming challenges from second-class constraints and representation reducibility.
AI.method: Uses BRST-BFV formalism: starts from a Fock-space realization of a Poincaré module; applies Verma module construction to identify auxiliary representations of the constraint subalgebra; exploits Howe duality to map it to so(k,k); introduces new oscillator variables to convert second-class constraints into first-class; constructs both Q-invariant (unconstrained) and Q_c-invariant (constrained) Lagrangians with algebraic gauge conditions.
AI.result: Derives explicit metric-like Lagrangians for bosonic higher-spin fields Φ_{μ¹[ŝ₁],...,μᵏ[ŝₖ]} corresponding to arbitrary k-column Young tableaux Y[ŝ₁,...,ŝₖ]; obtains two dynamically equivalent formulations—one fully unconstrained (via Q), one constrained (via Q_c plus algebraic BRST-invariant conditions); establishes framework for consistent interactions.
AI.conclusion: A unified BRST-based Lagrangian formalism is achieved for generic integer higher-spin Poincaré representations described by multi-row antisymmetric tensor fields; the method resolves constraint classification via Howe duality and Verma modules, enabling consistent coupling schemes.

title: Scalar diquarks in the QCD vacuum
summary: While QCD fundamentally only depends on the values of the strong coupling and the quark masses, it exhibits a rich nonperturbative structure at low energies, where composite fields emerge as the relevant degrees of freedom. In this work, we present a first-principles framework that captures the transition from fundamental QCD to its low-energy sector in vacuum. It builds on the dynamical hadronization technique within the functional renormalization group approach to two-flavor QCD. In this framework, the low-energy constants relevant for effective models, including effective masses and coupling strengths, naturally emerge from the underlying renormalization group flow without introducing free parameters beyond those of QCD itself.
