We investigate the dynamical emergence of the pion, the $σ$-meson and the scalar diquark in both imaginary and real time, and determine a set of QCD low-energy constants which can be used to fix the free parameters of models of dense quark matter with a two-flavor color superconducting phase. In particular, this includes previously unknown properties of the scalar diquark. Our results provide important microscopic input for constraining color superconducting phases, which are expected to play a key role in our understanding of dense neutron star matter.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a first-principles framework using dynamical hadronization within the functional renormalization group to derive low-energy QCD constants—such as effective masses and couplings—for pions, σ-mesons, and scalar diquarks, enabling parameter-free modeling of two-flavor color superconductivity in dense matter.
AI.motivation: To bridge fundamental QCD with its low-energy effective description without introducing ad hoc parameters, especially for modeling color superconducting phases relevant to neutron star interiors.
AI.method: Dynamical hadronization within the functional renormalization group (FRG) applied to two-flavor QCD; computation of low-energy constants from RG flow in both imaginary and real time.
AI.result: Derivation of QCD-determined low-energy constants for pion, σ-meson, and scalar diquark; first ab initio determination of previously unknown scalar diquark properties; quantitative input for two-flavor color superconducting models.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides parameter-free, microscopic constraints on effective models of dense quark matter, significantly advancing predictive capability for color superconducting phases in neutron stars.

title: Primordial Black Holes: A Review of Formation and Evolution
comment: Invited Review for Special Issue to Commemorate 100 Years of Indian Journal of Physics (accepted for publication), 40 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables
summary: Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) have emerged as a leading non-particulate candidate for dark matter and a unique cosmological probe, a paradigm shift accelerated by the detection of anomalous binary mergers by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration. While the literature is rich with phenomenological constraints, the fundamental quantum and relativistic underpinnings governing PBH genesis and evolution often receive comparatively less emphasis. This review aims to bridge that gap by systematically detailing the physics of PBH formation and their subsequent evolutionary trajectory. We critically examine the hydrodynamic complexity of the early universe, establishing the relativistic thresholds for collapse, the non-linear race against sound in the primordial plasma, and the rigorous mathematical utility of the compaction function. Furthermore, by incorporating the dynamic nature of FLRW backgrounds, higher curvature corrections, and quantum backreaction via the memory burden effect, we challenge the standard hawking evaporation and show that extreme-curvature environments halt evaporation entirely, leaving Planck-scale relics that evade current extragalactic bounds. Finally, we map the multimessenger observational landscape, highlighting how the imminent search for sub-solar mass inspirals by next-generation gravitational wave observatories -- such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer -- could yield smoking-gun evidence for the PBH paradigm, ultimately transforming these primordial relics into unparalleled laboratories for high-energy physics.

AI.tldr: This review bridges the gap between phenomenological constraints and fundamental physics of Primordial Black Holes (PBHs), emphasizing relativistic hydrodynamics, non-linear collapse thresholds, compaction function formalism, and quantum/relativistic corrections—including curvature-induced evaporation suppression yielding stable Planck relics—while positioning next-gen gravitational-wave observatories as decisive probes for sub-solar-mass PBHs.
AI.motivation: To address the underemphasis on quantum and relativistic foundations in PBH formation and evolution literature, despite their growing relevance as dark matter candidates and cosmological probes following anomalous LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA merger detections.
AI.method: Systematic theoretical analysis integrating relativistic hydrodynamics, non-linear collapse criteria in primordial plasma, compaction function formalism, FLRW background dynamics, higher-curvature gravity corrections, and quantum backreaction via the memory burden effect to reassess Hawking evaporation.
AI.result: Demonstration that extreme spacetime curvature halts Hawking evaporation entirely, leading to stable Planck-scale PBH relics that evade current extragalactic observational bounds; identification of sub-solar-mass PBH inspirals as 'smoking-gun' multimessenger signatures accessible to Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.
AI.conclusion: PBHs are not only viable dark matter candidates but also high-energy physics laboratories; their formation and fate must be understood through rigorous relativistic and quantum-gravitational frameworks, and upcoming gravitational-wave observatories offer transformative discovery potential.

title: A symmetry reduction of the Painlevé IV hierarchy to the Flaschka-Newell Painlevé II hierarchy
summary: We study the isomonodromic deformation problem associated with rank-two meromorphic connections on the Riemann sphere having one regular singularity and one irregular singularity of even order at infinity, corresponding to the even Painlevé IV hierarchy. We show that the symmetry $Ψ(-λ)= σ_1 Ψ(λ) σ_1$ defines an invariant submanifold whose induced isomonodromic dynamics coincides with the Flaschka-Newell Painlevé II hierarchy. Under this identification, the corresponding Lax matrices, Darboux coordinates and Hamiltonian structures can be matched explicitly. In particular, the Hamiltonians of the first members of the Flaschka-Newell hierarchy are recovered from the even Painlevé IV hierarchy. This provides a geometric interpretation of the Flaschka-Newell hierarchy as a symmetry reduction of an isomonodromic deformation problem, complementing its classical description as a similarity reduction of the modified Korteweg-de Vries hierarchy.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a geometric link between the even Painlevé IV hierarchy and the Flaschka-Newell Painlevé II hierarchy via symmetry reduction of an isomonodromic deformation problem for rank-two meromorphic connections on ℂℙ¹ with one regular and one even-order irregular singularity at ∞.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric interpretation of the Flaschka-Newell Painlevé II hierarchy—as a symmetry reduction of an isomonodromic deformation problem—complementing its known derivation from mKdV similarity reduction.
AI.method: Analysis of isomonodromic deformations of rank-2 meromorphic SL(2,ℂ) connections on ℂℙ¹ with prescribed singularity structure; imposition of the involution symmetry Ψ(−λ) = σ₁Ψ(λ)σ₁ to define an invariant submanifold; explicit matching of Lax matrices, Darboux coordinates, and Hamiltonian structures between hierarchies.
AI.result: The Flaschka-Newell Painlevé II hierarchy arises as the induced isomonodromic dynamics on the symmetry-invariant submanifold; Lax pairs, canonical coordinates, and Hamiltonians (including first members) are explicitly matched between the hierarchies.
AI.conclusion: The Flaschka-Newell hierarchy admits a novel geometric realization as a symmetry reduction of the even Painlevé IV isomonodromy problem, unifying perspectives from integrable systems, isomonodromic deformations, and Painlevé theory.

title: Null limit of large-charge correlators in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super-Yang-Mills theory
summary: We present a conjecture for the double-logarithmic behavior of the logarithm of large-charge correlators in the null limit in planar $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super-Yang-Mills theory. Generalizing earlier results for four- and five-point functions, our proposal predicts this behavior for $n$-point functions to all loops in terms of the tilted cusp anomalous dimension. In the dual amplitude description, it reproduces the expected small-mass behavior of massive amplitudes in the equal-mass limit.

AI.tldr: Proposes a conjecture for double-logarithmic behavior of large-charge correlators in the null limit of planar N=4 SYM, expressed via the tilted cusp anomalous dimension, and matches small-mass behavior of massive amplitudes in the equal-mass limit.
AI.motivation: To generalize earlier results on four- and five-point functions to n-point functions and unify large-charge correlator behavior with dual amplitude predictions in the equal-mass limit.
AI.method: Conjectural analysis based on symmetry, integrability, and known limits (null, large charge, equal mass), leveraging the tilted cusp anomalous dimension as the central object.
AI.result: A universal double-logarithmic form for log(correlators) in the null limit for arbitrary n-point functions at all loops, consistent with dual amplitude expectations for massive amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The conjecture bridges large-charge operator product expansion in correlators with infrared behavior of massive amplitudes, supporting integrability-based universality in planar N=4 SYM.

title: Multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational waves from PBH-assisted leptogenesis
summary: We study the possibility of probing non-thermal leptogenesis with multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational waves (GW) by considering heavy right-handed neutrino (RHN) produced from primordial black hole (PBH) evaporation to be responsible for generating the required lepton asymmetry. The decay of RHN also produces a GW spectrum due to graviton bremsstrahlung with the corresponding amplitude being enhanced for heavier RHN. The presence of an ultra-light PBH dominated epoch not only ensures sufficient production of RHNs, but also keeps the leptogenesis scenario free from strong washout problem of thermal leptogenesis at very high scale. In addition, the PBH dominated epoch also helps in generating a gravitational bremsstrahlung spectrum distinct from the stochastic GW background from the thermal bath. Finally, PBH evaporation also brings two separate sources of GW via density perturbation and graviton emission via Hawking evaporation. For the most optimistic scenario with very high scale seesaw consistent with neutrino mass and leptogenesis, this leads to a multi-peaked GW spectrum with peak frequencies lying in the MHz-EHz range.

AI.tldr: This paper explores non-thermal leptogenesis via heavy right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) produced from primordial black hole (PBH) evaporation, generating a multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational wave (GW) spectrum (MHz–EHz) through graviton bremsstrahlung and PBH-related mechanisms.
AI.motivation: To probe non-thermal leptogenesis via observable high-frequency gravitational waves, circumventing limitations of thermal leptogenesis (e.g., strong washout at high scales) and leveraging PBH evaporation as a controllable RHN production mechanism.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of RHN production from PBH evaporation during an ultra-light PBH-dominated epoch; computation of GW spectra from graviton bremsstrahlung in RHN decay, density perturbations, and Hawking radiation; spectral superposition to obtain multi-peaked GW signal.
AI.result: A distinct, multi-peaked GW spectrum in the MHz–EHz range emerges, separable from thermal stochastic background; peak structure encodes RHN mass, PBH mass distribution, and leptogenesis scale; viability demonstrated for high-scale seesaw consistent with neutrino masses and observed baryon asymmetry.
AI.conclusion: Multi-peaked high-frequency GWs from PBH-evaporation-driven non-thermal leptogenesis provide a novel, testable signature—potentially accessible to future resonant-mass or quantum-sensor-based GW detectors—and offer a pathway to indirectly probe high-scale physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Energy Extraction via Magnetic Reconnection from a Rotating Dyonic Black Hole in $N = 2, \ U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity
summary: We study energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating dyonic black hole in four-dimensional $N=2$, $U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity. Using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism in the ZAMO frame, we derive the asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy $ε^{\infty}_\pm$ and determine when reconnection outflows attained negative energy at infinity. By varying the spin $a$, electric and magnetic charges, NUT parameter $N_g$, and gauge coupling $g$, we compute the cutoff magnetization $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and map the region of parameter space that admits $ε^{\infty}_-<0$. We find that $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $Ξ$, and the quartic horizon function $Δ_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates magnetic reconnection–driven energy extraction from rotating dyonic black holes in 4D N=2 U(1)² gauged supergravity, generalizing the Comisso–Asenjo mechanism; it identifies parameter regimes (gauge coupling g, dyonic charges, spin a, NUT parameter Ng) where negative-energy outflows—and thus net energy extraction—are possible, revealing non-monotonic efficiency peaking at intermediate spin and strong dependence on AdS/NUT geometry over frame-dragging.
AI.motivation: To extend the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection energy extraction mechanism beyond Kerr black holes to more general rotating dyonic black holes in gauged supergravity—incorporating electric/magnetic charges, NUT charge, and cosmological (AdS) effects—and determine how these parameters influence feasibility and efficiency of energy extraction.
AI.method: Analyzes energy extraction via magnetic reconnection in the ZAMO (zero-angular-momentum observer) frame; computes asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy ε^∞_±; determines conditions for ε^∞_− < 0 (negative-energy outflows); numerically maps parameter space (a, Q, P, Ng, g) to identify cutoff magnetization σ₀^cutoff and regions supporting Comisso-Asenjo extraction; accounts for horizon geometry via Δ_g and normalization Ξ.
AI.result: σ₀^cutoff and existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are strongly controlled by gauge coupling g and dyonic charges—increasing g or approaching extremality raises σ₀^cutoff and shrinks the active ergoregion; spin a affects extraction non-monotonically via Ξ and Δ_g, with peak efficiency near a ∼ 0.8—not maximal spin; high efficiency requires extreme magnetization and near-radial outflows, confining reconnection to a thin shell just outside the horizon.
AI.conclusion: Energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from rotating dyonic black holes in gauged supergravity is viable but highly sensitive to gauge coupling and charge structure; geometric effects from AdS/NUT deformations dominate over frame-dragging, enabling efficient extraction at intermediate spin—challenging the paradigm that near-extremal rotation is necessary.

title: Long-time asymptotics of the autocorrelation function of the transverse Ising chain at the critical magnetic field Revisited
summary: Following the work of Deift and Zhou (DOI:10.1007/978-1-4615-2474-8_15), we analyze the long-time asymptotics of the autocorrelation function of the transverse Ising chain at the critical magnetic field (a special case of the spin-$\frac12$ XY model in a magnetic field) via the associated Riemann-Hilbert problem. We refine the original Deift-Zhou's result by determining the subleading growing term in the asymptotics.

AI.tldr: This paper refines the long-time asymptotics of the autocorrelation function for the critical transverse Ising chain using the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for Riemann–Hilbert problems, explicitly identifying the subleading growing term beyond the leading-order behavior.
AI.motivation: To improve upon Deift and Zhou's asymptotic analysis by capturing finer asymptotic structure—specifically, the subleading growing term—in the autocorrelation function of the critical transverse Ising chain, a paradigmatic quantum integrable model.
AI.method: Nonlinear steepest descent analysis of the associated matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem, building on the Deift–Zhou framework with refined parametrix construction and error estimation to extract subleading asymptotics.
AI.result: The long-time asymptotics of the autocorrelation function are determined up to and including the subleading growing term, which was not captured in the original Deift–Zhou analysis.
AI.conclusion: The subleading asymptotic contribution is rigorously established, enhancing the precision of the large-time description of correlation dynamics at quantum criticality in the transverse Ising model.

title: Equivariant Interpolations in Topological Holography
summary: We revisit equivariant Gromov-Witten theories on P1 and on P1 x C2. One can introduce three equivariant parameters associated to rotations of the sphere as well as the two planes. A number of points in the parameter space have known holographic duals. These include the symmetric orbifold point dual to the AdS3 x S3 x C2 string theory at string scale radius of curvature, the grand canonical Hurwitz theory and the product of two Kontsevich models. Within this framework, we discuss interpolations in the equivariant parameters. Firstly, we move between the small and large equivariant parameter regimes in Gromov-Witten theory on P1. At large equivariant parameter, the model is dominated by the pure topological gravity theories at the two fixed points while at small equivariant parameter the theory is equivalent to the grand canonical Hurwitz theory. The deformation is a solvable analogue for the interpolation in the transposition coupling in the moduli space of the AdS3/CFT2 duality. Moreover, we propose that the full equivariant correspondence between the Gromov-Witten theory on P1 x C2 and the symmetric orbifold of the equivariant plane can be embedded in string theory. On the boundary side of that correspondence, we analyze the scaling limit from the equivariant to the ordinary cohomology ring for the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane in terms of Jack symmetric polynomials. We explicitly compute several structure constants of the equivariant cohomology ring and point out their intriguing positivity and integrality properties.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits equivariant Gromov-Witten theories on P1 and P1 × C², explores interpolations between regimes via equivariant parameters, connects them to holographic duals (e.g., AdS₃/CFT₂, Hurwitz theory, Kontsevich models), proposes a string-theoretic embedding of the P1 × C² / symmetric orbifold correspondence, and analyzes the equivariant-to-ordinary cohomology limit for Hilbert schemes using Jack polynomials, revealing positivity and integrality of structure constants.
AI.motivation: To unify and interpolate between known holographic dualities—such as AdS₃×S³×C², grand canonical Hurwitz theory, and Kontsevich models—via equivariant Gromov-Witten theory, and to elucidate the role of equivariant parameters in moduli space deformations analogous to transposition coupling in AdS₃/CFT₂.
AI.method: Analyzes equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants on P¹ and P¹×C² with three rotation-equivariant parameters; studies limits (small/large parameters); identifies holographic correspondences; embeds the P¹×C² / symmetric orbifold equivalence in string theory; computes equivariant cohomology ring structure constants for Hilbert schemes of points on C² using Jack symmetric polynomials and examines their combinatorial properties.
AI.result: Establishes solvable interpolations between topological gravity at fixed points (large parameter) and grand canonical Hurwitz theory (small parameter); proposes string-theoretic realization of the equivariant P¹×C² / symmetric orbifold duality; derives explicit structure constants of the equivariant cohomology ring exhibiting positivity and integrality; links scaling limits to Jack polynomial expansions.
AI.conclusion: Equivariant parameters provide a unifying geometric and physical framework connecting diverse dualities; the interpolation behavior mirrors AdS₃/CFT₂ moduli deformations; the integrality/positivity of cohomological structure constants suggests deep algebraic–geometric or representation-theoretic origins tied to Jack polynomials.

title: One Generator, Any Process: LLM-Conditioning for the LHC
summary: Neural network training for LHC event generation should, ideally, benefit from common high-level patterns in different processes. We propose novel conditioning schemes for continuous parameters, process labels, and Feynman diagrams. We employ pre-trained LLMs as multi-modal foundation models to provide descriptive embeddings for an autoregressive transformer. With such high-level physics-inductive bias the generative networks converge faster, provide better result, and generalize to unseen processes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces novel conditioning schemes using pre-trained LLMs as multi-modal foundation models to embed high-level physics concepts (e.g., process labels, Feynman diagrams) for autoregressive transformers in LHC event generation—improving convergence speed, fidelity, and generalization to unseen processes.
AI.motivation: Neural network training for LHC event generation lacks explicit incorporation of high-level physics patterns across processes; leveraging such structure could improve efficiency and generalization.
AI.method: Proposes continuous-parameter conditioning, process-label conditioning, and Feynman-diagram conditioning; uses pre-trained large language models (LLMs) to generate descriptive, physics-informed embeddings fed into an autoregressive transformer architecture.
AI.result: Generative networks exhibit faster convergence, improved generation quality (e.g., physical fidelity, statistical agreement), and zero-shot or few-shot generalization to previously unseen particle physics processes.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating high-level physics-inductive bias via LLM-derived embeddings significantly enhances the performance and generalizability of generative models for collider event simulation.

title: Newtonian Shirokov Effect: Epicyclic Frequency Splitting from Mass Multipoles
summary: We analyze small oscillations of nearly circular orbits in an axisymmetric Newtonian potential expanded in mass multipoles, as the classical counterpart of the relativistic Shirokov effect. Computing the full Hessian of the effective potential at the true (possibly tilted) equilibrium and solving the coupled two-mode oscillator exactly, we obtain a complete picture. (i) A quadrupole splits the radial and vertical epicyclic frequencies, $Ω_θ^2-Ω_r^2=-3GQ/r_0^5=6GMJ_2R^2/r_0^5$, at first order in $J_2$; the Newtonian analogue of the Shirokov splitting, equivalent to the classical statement that an oblate body's apsidal and nodal rates differ. (ii) A gravitational dipole produces no splitting: it equals $M r_{\rm CM}$, is removable by re-centering at the center of mass, and cannot appear in any coordinate-independent frequency; the apparent first-order coupling cancels at the true tilted equilibrium, any residual absorbed by the induced quadrupole of the shifted source, confirmed by direct orbit integration. (iii) A genuine octupole does split the frequencies, $ω_+^2-ω_-^2\approx6G|O|/r_0^6$. The selection rule is thus not even/odd parity: every multipole splits the frequencies except the dipole. These yield two complementary probes of an axisymmetric source: the frequency splitting measures the oblateness $J_2$, while the orbital-plane tilt, $δθ_0\simeq-r_{\rm CM}/r_0$, measures the center-of-mass offset $r_{\rm CM}$, an orbital-geometry observable rather than a frequency one. We give solar-system estimates for both. Carried through to Shirokov's original observable -- the secular transverse drift after $n$ orbits -- the quadrupole effect gives $ξ^θ=ξ_0^θ\,πn\,(6J_2R^2/r_0^2)$, of order $10^{-8}$ cm at $1$ au and $\sim10^{-6}$ cm near $0.1$ au, comparable to Shirokov's Schwarzschild estimate.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes small oscillations of nearly circular orbits in axisymmetric Newtonian potentials, identifying how mass multipoles (especially quadrupole and octupole) split epicyclic frequencies—providing classical analogues to the relativistic Shirokov effect—and showing that dipole contributions vanish at true equilibrium, while orbital-plane tilt measures center-of-mass offset.
AI.motivation: To establish the classical Newtonian counterpart of the relativistic Shirokov effect—specifically, how mass multipole moments of an axisymmetric gravitational source affect epicyclic frequency splitting and orbital precession—and clarify misconceptions about dipole contributions.
AI.method: Computes the full Hessian of the effective potential at the true (possibly tilted) equilibrium orbit; solves the coupled two-mode oscillator exactly; expands the potential in mass multipoles (monopole, dipole, quadrupole, octupole); performs direct orbit integration to verify cancellation of dipole effects; derives frequency splittings and orbital-geometry observables (e.g., tilt angle).
AI.result: Quadrupole (J₂) splits radial and vertical epicyclic frequencies: Ω_θ² − Ω_r² = 6GMJ₂R²/r₀⁵; dipole contributes no observable splitting—it vanishes at true tilted equilibrium and is absorbed into induced quadrupole; octupole induces measurable splitting ω₊² − ω₋² ≈ 6G|O|/r₀⁶; orbital-plane tilt δθ₀ ≈ −r_CM/r₀ directly measures center-of-mass offset; solar-system estimates provided for both J₂-induced splitting and r_CM-induced tilt.
AI.conclusion: The frequency splitting is governed by a selection rule excluding only the dipole—every higher multipole contributes, refuting even/odd parity arguments; quadrupole splitting probes oblateness J₂, while orbital tilt probes center-of-mass offset r_CM; this yields two independent, complementary observational constraints on axisymmetric mass distributions, with quantitative predictions comparable to Shirokov’s relativistic estimates.

title: Data-Based Dynamical Systems Reconstruction: An Adequacy/Reliability Test
summary: In this work, we address the problem of validating the reconstruction of a stochastic system from noisy data. We demonstrate the limitations of criteria based solely on the loss function or on standard metrics used for reconstructing deterministic dynamics. We also propose an exploratory approach, based on a two-step test, which allows for a general assessment of the reconstruction without relying on arbitrary error-tolerance thresholds. However, we discuss how system degeneracy and non-identifiability, together with features intrinsic to stochastic dynamics, impose certain constraints on the application of this test.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses validation of stochastic system reconstruction from noisy data, critiques conventional loss- and deterministic-metric-based criteria, and proposes a two-step exploratory test for general assessment—while acknowledging constraints from system degeneracy, non-identifiability, and intrinsic stochasticity.
AI.motivation: To overcome the inadequacy of standard loss-based or deterministic-metric-based validation criteria when reconstructing stochastic systems from noisy data.
AI.method: Proposes a two-step exploratory test for general assessment of stochastic system reconstruction, avoiding arbitrary error-tolerance thresholds; analyzes limitations imposed by system degeneracy, non-identifiability, and stochastic dynamics.
AI.result: Demonstrates fundamental limitations of conventional validation criteria and establishes a more principled, threshold-free framework—albeit with acknowledged constraints on applicability due to structural and dynamical properties of stochastic systems.
AI.conclusion: Validation of stochastic reconstructions requires criteria beyond deterministic analogs; the proposed two-step test offers a more robust exploratory approach, but its utility is bounded by inherent identifiability and degeneracy issues in stochastic modeling.

title: Topics in Celestial holography: A bottom-up perspective
summary: We review some selected topics in celestial holography on the search for a celestial dual to quantum gravity in flat spacetimes. We focus on the bottom-up approach, emphasizing symmetries, key elements in celestial CFT, interplay with twistor theory, and connection to AdS/CFT.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews selected topics in celestial holography aimed at identifying a celestial dual for quantum gravity in flat spacetimes, adopting a bottom-up approach centered on symmetries, celestial CFT foundations, twistor theory links, and AdS/CFT connections.
AI.motivation: To advance the search for a holographic dual of quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes via celestial holography.
AI.method: Bottom-up theoretical review focusing on symmetry structures (e.g., BMS, Virasoro extensions), celestial conformal field theory formalism, twistor correspondence, and comparative analysis with AdS/CFT.
AI.result: Synthesizes conceptual and technical progress in celestial holography, clarifying roles of asymptotic symmetries, soft theorems, memory effects, and twistorial formulations in constructing a putative celestial CFT.
AI.conclusion: Celestial holography remains a promising but incomplete framework; key challenges include defining a unitary, local celestial CFT and establishing a rigorous bulk reconstruction map for flat space quantum gravity.

title: Nuclei in high-energy neutrino sources: A multimessenger study of in-source propagation
summary: The joint observation of astrophysical sources in gamma rays and neutrinos can provide invaluable insight into the physical conditions of the source, including its size, particle densities, and acceleration and production mechanisms. In this work, we investigate the role of nuclear composition in high-energy astrophysical environments. Using NGC 1068 as a representative example, we perform detailed Monte Carlo simulations of nuclear and electromagnetic cascades within the source and study the imprints of the injected nuclear composition on the resulting neutrino and gamma-ray emissions. We further discuss the importance of MeV-GeV gamma-ray observations for constraining the source composition in the context of future gamma-ray experiments. A dedicated re-analysis of archival COMPTEL observations is also presented.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how nuclear composition affects neutrino and gamma-ray emissions from high-energy astrophysical sources, using NGC 1068 as a test case with Monte Carlo cascade simulations, and emphasizes the diagnostic power of MeV–GeV gamma-ray data for composition inference.
AI.motivation: To understand how nuclear composition influences multi-messenger (neutrino + gamma-ray) signatures from astrophysical sources, enabling constraints on source physical conditions such as size, particle densities, and acceleration mechanisms.
AI.method: Detailed Monte Carlo simulations of nuclear and electromagnetic cascades within NGC 1068; re-analysis of archival COMPTEL MeV gamma-ray data; theoretical modeling of composition-dependent neutrino and gamma-ray spectral imprints.
AI.result: Injected nuclear composition leaves distinct imprints on the energy spectra and flux ratios of neutrinos and gamma rays; MeV–GeV gamma-ray observations are shown to be critical for breaking degeneracies in composition inference.
AI.conclusion: Nuclear composition is a key observable in multi-messenger astrophysics; future MeV–GeV gamma-ray missions (e.g., AMEGO, e-ASTROGAM) will significantly enhance our ability to constrain source composition and underlying physics.

title: Nonrotating and rotating black holes with secondary disformal hair in a ghost-free metric-affine parity-violating scalar-torsion theory
summary: In this paper, we formulate a ghost-free metric-affine scalar-torsion model in which a pseudoscalar field is coupled to the Nieh--Yan density and derivatively coupled to the Einstein-Palatini tensor. The theory is projectively invariant and, in the shift-symmetric sector, depends on the scalar only through its gradient. After fixing the projective gauge, the independent connection is solved exactly: its symmetric part is the Levi-Civita connection associated with the metric \(h_{μν}\), disformally related to the metric $g_{μν}$, while its antisymmetric part is a purely axial torsion sourced by $v_μ=\partial_μ\vartheta$. We identify a degenerate ghost-free branch, $α=6β^2κ^2$, for which Ricci-flat geometries in the $h$-metric frame solve the metric equations and the Noether current vanishes identically. For example, we consider Schwarzschild and Kerr geometries in the $h$-metric frame, which generate disformal deformations on these geometries from the perspective of the $g$-metric frame. For the Schwarzschild black hole in the $h$-metric frame, we construct static and Babichev--Charmousis-like time-dependent scalar profiles, and discuss horizon regularity in Eddington--Finkelstein coordinates. For the Kerr black hole in the $h$-metric frame, we show that the fixed-norm scalar profile is generically axisymmetric, depending on both the radial and angular coordinates, and we construct a stationary future-regular profile in ingoing Kerr coordinates. The Kerr solution with the nontrivial scalar field is stealth only in the $h$-metric frame. In the $g$-metric frame, it produces disformal corrections stemming from the nontrivial scalar field profile and it represents secondary disformal scalar hair rather than primary Noether-charge hair.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a ghost-free metric-affine scalar-torsion theory where a pseudoscalar couples to the Nieh–Yan density and derivatively to the Einstein–Palatini tensor; it exhibits projective invariance, yields exact connection solutions (Levi-Civita + axial torsion), identifies a degenerate ghost-free parameter branch, and derives disformally deformed Schwarzschild/Kerr black holes with stealth scalar profiles in the h-frame and secondary scalar hair in the g-frame.
AI.motivation: To formulate a consistent, ghost-free extension of gravity incorporating torsion and a pseudoscalar field while preserving projective invariance and avoiding Ostrogradsky instabilities.
AI.method: Constructs a metric-affine action with pseudoscalar coupling to Nieh–Yan density and derivative coupling to Einstein–Palatini tensor; imposes projective invariance and shift symmetry; solves connection equations exactly; analyzes degeneracy conditions for ghost freedom; studies black hole solutions (Schwarzschild/Kerr) in both h- and g-metric frames using Eddington–Finkelstein and ingoing Kerr coordinates.
AI.result: Derives exact connection solution: symmetric part is Levi-Civita of disformally related metric h_μν, antisymmetric part is axial torsion ∝ ∂_μϑ; identifies ghost-free branch α = 6β²κ²; shows Ricci-flat h-metric solutions satisfy field equations with vanishing Noether current; constructs static and time-dependent scalar profiles for Schwarzschild; finds axisymmetric, stationary, future-regular scalar profile for Kerr; establishes stealth behavior in h-frame but secondary disformal hair in g-frame.
AI.conclusion: The model provides a consistent, projectively invariant, ghost-free scalar-torsion theory yielding physically viable black hole solutions with disformal scalar hair—non-Noetherian, secondary, and frame-dependent—thereby enriching the landscape of modified gravity with torsion and pseudoscalar fields.

title: Dark-Sector Deformations of Holographic Anisotropic Superfluids in Asymptotically Hyperscaling Violation Geometry
summary: We study dark-sector deformations of holographic anisotropic \(p\)-wave superfluids in hyperscaling-violating black-brane backgrounds. In the visible \(SU(2)\) sector, \(b(u)\) fixes the chemical potential and charge density, while \(ω(u)\) condenses and selects a boundary direction, producing anisotropic strip entanglement. The visible critical chemical potential, radial profiles, condensate branch, and strip-entanglement difference vary with dimension and hyperscaling-violating exponents. We then add hidden gauge sectors and hidden dark-scalar portals. Hidden-current mixing gives a solvable example, whereas isotropic dark sources cancel in the strip difference. For the kinetic dark-scalar portal, \(Z_{\rm dm}(Φ)\) deforms the Yang--Mills operator; hence \(b_0(u)\), \(ω_1(u)\), and the order-\(ε^2\) anisotropic stress are computed in the same deformed problem. The critical shift depends on the hyperscaling-violating background and can change sign. The main result is a strip susceptibility at vanishing portal strength. It is negative in the \(D=4\) and \(D=5\) backgrounds, so the portal weakly suppresses visible strip anisotropy. This has a holographic RG interpretation: the normalizable dark scalar is weighted toward the IR horizon, while narrow strips probe the UV near-boundary RT region. Thus, the portal decouples in the UV and the susceptibility vanishes quadratically with strip width; wider strips reach deeper into the bulk and recover the IR dark-sector effects.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how dark-sector deformations affect holographic anisotropic p-wave superfluids in hyperscaling-violating black-brane geometries, focusing on entanglement strip anisotropy and its response to hidden-sector couplings—finding a negative strip susceptibility at vanishing portal strength, indicating UV decoupling of dark scalars.
AI.motivation: To understand how dark-sector physics (hidden gauge fields and dark scalars) influences observable anisotropic quantum critical phenomena—specifically entanglement structure—in strongly coupled holographic superfluids.
AI.method: Holographic renormalization and perturbative bulk analysis in hyperscaling-violating black-brane backgrounds; computation of radial profiles, condensate branches, and strip entanglement entropy differences; inclusion of hidden-current mixing and kinetic dark-scalar portals via deformed Yang–Mills and scalar kinetic terms.
AI.result: The strip entanglement susceptibility to dark-scalar portal strength is negative in D=4 and D=5, implying suppression of visible anisotropy; it vanishes quadratically with strip width due to IR-localization of the normalizable dark scalar versus UV-probing nature of narrow strips.
AI.conclusion: Dark-sector effects on visible anisotropic entanglement are suppressed at small strip widths due to holographic RG separation between UV boundary probes and IR-localized dark degrees of freedom—providing a geometric mechanism for dark-sector screening in entanglement observables.

title: PDF evolution in alternative factorisation schemes
summary: Beyond leading order, parton distribution functions (PDFs) require a choice of factorisation scheme to be defined unambiguously. Different choices of factorisation scheme lead to PDFs that satisfy modified DGLAP evolution equations, relative to the conventional $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme. In this paper we derive the NLO DGLAP splitting functions for PDFs in alternative factorisation schemes, including for a parametrised scheme spanning a subspace of the general factorisation-scheme space. We plot their Mellin-space counterparts, the anomalous dimensions, and study the leading large- and small-$x$ behaviour, relevant to resummation. We find that the leading behaviour admits a natural interpretation as a modified effective evolution scale. This is an essential step towards being able to evolve and fit PDFs in alternative schemes for use within QCD calculations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives NLO DGLAP splitting functions for parton distribution functions (PDFs) in arbitrary factorisation schemes beyond $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$, analyzes their Mellin-space anomalous dimensions, and interprets leading large- and small-$x$ behaviour in terms of a modified effective evolution scale.
AI.motivation: PDFs beyond leading order depend on the choice of factorisation scheme; unambiguous definition and consistent evolution require scheme-specific DGLAP kernels, yet systematic derivation and analysis of such kernels—especially at NLO—are lacking.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of NLO DGLAP splitting functions for general factorisation schemes using operator renormalisation and consistency with QCD gauge invariance; Mellin transformation to obtain anomalous dimensions; asymptotic analysis of large-$x$ and small-$x$ limits.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for NLO splitting functions in arbitrary schemes; Mellin-space anomalous dimensions plotted and classified by asymptotic behaviour; identification of a scheme-dependent effective evolution scale governing leading-logarithmic resummation.
AI.conclusion: The derived splitting functions enable consistent NLO evolution and global PDF fits in non-$\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ schemes, facilitating improved theoretical flexibility and precision in QCD predictions.

title: Nanohertz gravitational waves from domain walls nucleated during inflation
summary: We investigate scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) produced by domain walls (DWs) nucleated via quantum tunneling during inflation with an extended nucleation time. In contrast to the small-period nucleation framework, where DWs form instantaneously and produce a curvature power spectrum too weak to account for the nanohertz stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) reported by pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations, we show that a finite nucleation duration leads to a distribution of DW radii characterized by $γ\equiv\overline{R^4}/(\overline{R^2})^2>1$, which enhances the resulting curvature perturbations. We construct a two-field inflation model with an inflaton $φ$ and a spectator field $χ$ coupled through the potential $V(φ,χ)$, where the DW tension $σ(t)$ evolves smoothly as the inflaton rolls past a critical value. The characteristic width of this transition determines the cutoff scale $k_{\text{cut}}$ of the curvature power spectrum, enabling the SIGW peak to be placed in the nanohertz frequency band with detectable amplitude. For three representative parameter sets, we compute the SIGW spectra and find that the nanohertz-peaked spectrum matching the NANOGrav and EPTA signals. By selecting different parameters, our model simultaneously predicts potentially observable signals at other gravitational-wave detectors.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-field inflation model where domain walls nucleate over an extended time via quantum tunneling, leading to enhanced scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) peaking in the nanohertz band—consistent with PTA observations (NANOGrav/EPTA) and potentially detectable by other GW observatories.
AI.motivation: To explain the nanohertz stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) reported by pulsar timing arrays, which cannot be accounted for by instantaneous domain wall formation models due to insufficient curvature perturbations.
AI.method: Constructs a two-field inflation model (inflaton φ + spectator χ) with smoothly evolving domain wall tension σ(t); computes curvature power spectrum with finite nucleation duration; derives SIGW spectra using second-order cosmological perturbation theory; analyzes spectral shape, peak frequency, and amplitude dependence on nucleation width and field couplings.
AI.result: Extended nucleation yields γ > 1 (nontrivial radius distribution), enhancing curvature perturbations; cutoff scale k_cut tunes SIGW peak into nanohertz band; three benchmark parameter sets reproduce NANOGrav and EPTA SGWB amplitudes; model also predicts observable signals for LISA, DECIGO, and ET.
AI.conclusion: Finite-duration domain wall nucleation during inflation provides a viable, testable mechanism for generating the observed PTA SGWB via scalar-induced gravitational waves, bridging inflationary physics and multi-band gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: Exact and Finite de Sitter QFT from CFT
summary: Parallel to the AdS Scale-Space construction in \cite{Yang:2026AdS}, we construct a $(d+1)$-dimensional de Sitter QFT directly from $d$-dimensional CFT data. The dS geometry is the moduli space of oriented balls, and the lifted operators are obtained by conformal-family Casimir completion. The Euclidean parent CFT gives a finite wavefunction representation, while the Minkowski parent CFT gives a double-time representation that is unitary in the parent-time polarization. This provides a CFT-based framework for reexamining puzzles of dS and double-time QFT.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a (d+1)-dimensional de Sitter quantum field theory from d-dimensional CFT data, using oriented balls' moduli space as dS geometry and conformal-family Casimir completion for operator lifting; it yields finite wavefunction (Euclidean) or unitary double-time (Minkowski) representations, offering a CFT-based approach to dS and double-time QFT puzzles.
AI.motivation: To provide a CFT-based framework for addressing foundational puzzles in de Sitter quantum field theory and double-time QFT, by extending the AdS scale-space construction to dS.
AI.method: Constructs a (d+1)-dimensional dS QFT from d-dimensional CFT data, interpreting dS geometry as the moduli space of oriented balls and lifting operators via conformal-family Casimir completion; distinguishes Euclidean (finite wavefunction) vs. Minkowski (unitary double-time) parent CFT realizations.
AI.result: A well-defined dS QFT construction with two complementary representations: a finite wavefunction representation from Euclidean CFT, and a unitary double-time representation—unitary in parent-time polarization—from Minkowski CFT.
AI.conclusion: The construction establishes a rigorous CFT-derived dS QFT, enabling systematic reexamination of dS holography and double-time formalism, and generalizes the AdS scale-space paradigm to de Sitter spacetime.

title: Nonlinear Stability of Kerr-Sen Black Holes in Merging Binaries
summary: We investigate the stability of Kerr-Sen black holes, which arise in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion theory. Within a numerical relativity framework, we perform head-on binary black hole simulations with approximate initial data across a portion of the parameter space. We find that for nontrivial electric charge, a dilaton field persists through merger and that in the presence of spin, the remnant will also retain an axion field. The persistence of these fields for long times after merger strongly suggests the stability of these black holes within this alternative gravity theory. We further test whether initially unscalarized black holes will acquire hair in the presence of a scalar background. We find that black holes immersed in such a background retain scalar hair. Furthermore, we find that even initially unscalarized Kerr-Newman black holes will scalarize and remain scalarized throughout the evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically investigates the stability of Kerr-Sen black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion theory via head-on binary mergers, finding persistent dilaton and axion fields post-merger—indicating stability—and demonstrates spontaneous scalarization of initially unscalarized black holes in scalar backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To test the stability of Kerr-Sen black holes—a rotating, charged, scalar-hairy solution in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory—and to probe spontaneous scalarization dynamics in scalar-field backgrounds.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulations of head-on binary black hole mergers using approximate initial data spanning a subset of the Kerr-Sen parameter space; includes evolution of dilaton, axion, and electromagnetic fields; tests scalarization onset by immersing unscalarized black holes in external scalar backgrounds.
AI.result: Dilaton field persists post-merger for nonzero electric charge; axion field persists when spin is present; both persist for long times—supporting stability; unscalarized black holes (including Kerr-Newman) spontaneously scalarize and retain hair in scalar backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: Kerr-Sen black holes exhibit numerical evidence of stability in EMDA theory; spontaneous scalarization is robust—even for vacuum Kerr-Newman black holes immersed in scalar backgrounds—suggesting generic hair acquisition under suitable environmental conditions.

title: Canonical quantization for effective theories with higher-derivative perturbations: a covariant phase space approach
summary: The standard approach to canonical quantization encounters difficulties in dealing with higher-derivative perturbations that alter the kinetic structure of unperturbed theories. We show that the covariant phase space formalism provides a natural and technically efficient way to circumvent this obstruction. We illustrate the method with an exactly solvable model: a two-dimensional non-relativistic charged particle moving in a magnetic field and a harmonic confining potential, with its kinetic energy viewed as a perturbation. We quantize this model with covariant phase space formalism by constructing the solution perturbatively. We then calculate the energy spectrum and the unequal-time commutators of this system, and obtain the results that agree with the expansion of the exact theory. The procedure developed here is intended to serve as a systematic framework for the canonical quantization of more complex theories with higher-derivative perturbations.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using the covariant phase space formalism to canonically quantize theories with higher-derivative perturbations—where standard canonical quantization fails—and validates the approach on an exactly solvable 2D non-relativistic charged particle model.
AI.motivation: Standard canonical quantization struggles with higher-derivative perturbations that modify the kinetic structure; a robust, systematic alternative is needed.
AI.method: Applies the covariant phase space formalism to construct a perturbative quantization of a 2D non-relativistic charged particle in magnetic and harmonic potentials, treating kinetic energy as a perturbation.
AI.result: Obtains consistent energy spectrum and unequal-time commutators matching the exact theory’s expansion, confirming the formalism’s validity and consistency.
AI.conclusion: Covariant phase space formalism provides a natural, technically efficient, and systematic framework for canonical quantization of theories with higher-derivative perturbations.

title: Event isotropy in perturbative QCD
summary: It has recently been proposed that collider events can be equipped with a metric, the Energy Mover's Distance (EMD), which allows one to rephrase multiple aspects of collider physics in a geometric language. Further, the EMD can be exploited to define new observables. In this context, event isotropy quantifies the resemblance of an event to a uniform energy distribution. We present the first theoretical study of event isotropy within the framework of perturbative QCD. In particular, we first obtain the isotropy distribution in $e^+e^-$ collisions semi-analytically at $O(α_s)$ (leading-order) and numerically at $O(α_s^2)$ (next-to-leading order, NLO). Furthermore, we obtain all-order theoretical predictions by resumming the contributions of soft and collinear emissions, at next-to-leading logarithmic (NLL) accuracy. By matching resummed and fixed-order predictions we reach NLL+NLO accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces and theoretically studies 'event isotropy'—a new observable based on the Energy Mover's Distance (EMD)—in perturbative QCD, providing semi-analytic LO, numerical NLO, and resummed NLL predictions for its distribution in e⁺e⁻ collisions, culminating in a matched NLL+NLO result.
AI.motivation: To develop and theoretically ground event isotropy—a geometric observable derived from the Energy Mover's Distance—as a tool for quantifying how uniformly energy is distributed in collider events, enabling new insights in jet substructure and event shape analysis.
AI.method: Semi-analytical calculation at O(α_s) (LO) and numerical fixed-order computation at O(α_s²) (NLO) for event isotropy in e⁺e⁻ collisions; all-order resummation of soft and collinear emissions at next-to-leading logarithmic (NLL) accuracy; matching of resummed and fixed-order results to achieve NLL+NLO accuracy.
AI.result: First complete theoretical predictions for event isotropy distribution: LO semi-analytic form, NLO numerical cross section, NLL resummed spectrum, and matched NLL+NLO result with improved precision and reliability across energy scales.
AI.conclusion: Event isotropy is a well-defined, calculable observable in perturbative QCD; its distribution exhibits robust theoretical control up to NLL+NLO accuracy, validating its use as a geometric probe of event structure in high-energy collisions.

title: Low-mass X-ray binaries as a probe of Kerr-MOG black hole spacetime
summary: We investigate the astrophysical implications of rotating black holes in modified gravity by studying the Kerr-MOG spacetime and applying it to several stellar-mass black hole candidates: A0620-00, H1743-322, XTE J1550-564, GRS1124-683, GRO J1655-40, and GRS1915+105. The Kerr-MOG geometry is characterized by the black hole mass, the spin parameter $a$, and the modified gravity parameter $α$. We analyze how the presence of the MOG parameter modifies the spacetime structure and the location of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). Within the Novikov--Thorne accretion disk model, we show that $α$ significantly affects the radiative efficiency of accretion disks and introduces a degeneracy between the spin and the modified gravity parameter. Using observational estimates of radiative efficiencies inferred from the continuum-fitting method, we constrain the allowed regions in the $(a,α)$ parameter space for each source. We further examine the relativistic jet power using the Blandford--Znajek mechanism and compare the theoretical predictions with the observed transient jet energetics, considering two representative jet Lorentz factors, $Γ=2$ and $Γ=5$. By combining the constraints from the radiative efficiency and jet power, we identify regions where both observables can be simultaneously reproduced. For several sources significant overlap regions appear, while for the highly spinning source GRS1915+105 the compatibility occurs only within a narrow range of Kerr--MOG parameters. These results suggest that the Kerr--MOG spacetime can provide a viable framework for interpreting the observed properties of several black hole X-ray binaries.

AI.tldr: This paper studies rotating black holes in Modified Gravity (MOG) via the Kerr-MOG spacetime, constraining the MOG parameter α and spin a using radiative efficiency (from continuum-fitting) and relativistic jet power (Blandford–Znajek) for six stellar-mass black hole candidates; it finds viable (a, α) regions consistent with both observables, supporting Kerr-MOG as a plausible alternative framework.
AI.motivation: To test whether modified gravity—specifically Scalar–Tensor–Vector Gravity (STVG/MOG)—can consistently explain astrophysical observables of stellar-mass black holes without invoking general relativity alone, by exploring degeneracies between spin and the MOG parameter α.
AI.method: Analyzes Kerr-MOG metric properties (ISCO radius, ergoregion, frame-dragging); computes radiative efficiency in Novikov–Thorne thin-disk model; infers (a, α) constraints from observed efficiencies; calculates Blandford–Znajek jet power for Γ = 2 and Γ = 5; jointly constrains (a, α) space using both disk and jet observables.
AI.result: Significant overlapping allowed (a, α) regions found for A0620-00, H1743-322, XTE J1550-564, GRS1124-683, and GRO J1655-40; for GRS1915+105, compatibility is restricted to a narrow band due to its high inferred spin. Radiative efficiency exhibits strong degeneracy between a and α; jet power provides complementary, non-degenerate constraints.
AI.conclusion: Kerr-MOG spacetime remains astrophysically viable for multiple black hole X-ray binaries; joint modeling of accretion disk efficiency and jet energetics breaks parameter degeneracies and enables meaningful tests of MOG against GR using current observational data.

title: More on Kashaev limits of the quantum $A$-polynomials
summary: "Colored" knot polynomials satisfy difference equation w.r.t. the highest weights of the underlying representation -- which in the case of symmetrically colored Jones are named "quantum $A$-polynomials". In the double scaling quasiclassical (Kashaev) limit, when representation size $r\sim \hbar^{-1}$, there are different phases -- in one of them the classical action vanishes and in another one it is a deformation of hyperbolic volume (of a knot complement in $S^3$). This corresponds to a splitting of the non-homogeneous version of the quantum $A$-polynomial into two pieces, which we illustrate by more examples than just a figure-eight knot $4_1$ in the original paper. From the point of view of quasiclassics, hyperbolic volume is just an integration constant, which is not fully determined by the $A$-polynomial equation -- and actually remains ambiguous in this formalism. As a byproduct, we expect that classical $A$-polynomial at $L=1$ becomes proportional to Alexander: $A^{\cal K}(1,M)\sim Δ^{\cal K}(M)$ -- this seems true, but $A$ should be consistent with the polynomiality of {\it non-homogeneous quantum} ${\cal A}$-polynomial, what sometime implies that it is not minimal.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the quasiclassical limit of colored knot polynomials, focusing on quantum A-polynomials for symmetric representations; it identifies two distinct phases in the double-scaling limit (r ∼ ℏ⁻¹), links one phase’s classical action to hyperbolic volume (up to an undetermined integration constant), explains how the non-homogeneous quantum A-polynomial splits accordingly, and proposes a proportionality between the classical A-polynomial at L=1 and the Alexander polynomial — subject to consistency with quantum polynomiality constraints.
AI.motivation: To understand the structure and limits of quantum A-polynomials for colored knot invariants, especially their quasiclassical behavior and relation to geometric invariants like hyperbolic volume and the Alexander polynomial.
AI.method: Analysis of the difference equations satisfied by symmetrically colored Jones polynomials (quantum A-polynomials), examination of the double-scaling Kashaev limit (r ∼ ℏ⁻¹), phase decomposition of the classical action, and comparison with classical invariants including hyperbolic volume and Alexander polynomial.
AI.result: Two distinct quasiclassical phases emerge: one with vanishing classical action, another with action deforming hyperbolic volume; the non-homogeneous quantum A-polynomial splits accordingly; classical A-polynomial evaluated at L=1 is conjectured proportional to the Alexander polynomial, but minimality may be sacrificed to preserve quantum polynomiality.
AI.conclusion: The quantum A-polynomial encodes rich geometric and topological information in its quasiclassical limit, yet hyperbolic volume appears only as an ambiguous integration constant; the link to Alexander polynomial reveals constraints on classical A-polynomial minimality imposed by quantum consistency.

title: Multi-dimensional chaos II: String scattering amplitudes, curve repulsion, and RMT
summary: Multi-dimensional chaos refers to processes described by erratic functions of several dynamical variables. In this letter we analyze the string scattering amplitudes of highly-excited states and ground states. We show that the amplitudes, which depend on a scattering angle and a polarization angle, are characterized by two sets of non-intersecting curves associated with the vanishing of the derivatives with respect to the angles. We introduce the notion of the "area eigenvalue" $A_n$ associated with the $n$-th curve. We compute the spacings $δ_{n}= A_{n+1}-A_n$ and their ratios $r_{n}=\frac{δ_{n+1}}{δ_n}$. We show that the distributions of the spacing ratios take the form of the RMT Gaussian $β$-ensembles. The curves associated with the scattering angle tend to converge to the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble value of $β=1$ and those related to the polarization angle to the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble $β=2$. We also compute the ``areas form factor" associated with the areas and discover the regions of decline, ramp and plateau which characterize chaotic processes. The slope of the ramp seems to agree with the $β$ values extracted from the distribution of the spacing ratios.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates multi-dimensional chaos in string scattering amplitudes of highly-excited and ground states, identifying two families of non-intersecting critical curves (in scattering and polarization angles), defining 'area eigenvalues' A_n, analyzing spacing ratios r_n that follow RMT Gaussian β-ensembles (β≈1 for scattering-angle curves, β≈2 for polarization-angle curves), and computing an 'area form factor' exhibiting the universal three-regime structure (decline–ramp–plateau) characteristic of quantum chaos.
AI.motivation: To uncover signatures of multi-dimensional chaos in string theory scattering amplitudes by probing statistical properties of critical curves in parameter space.
AI.method: Analysis of string scattering amplitudes as functions of scattering and polarization angles; identification of critical curves via vanishing angular derivatives; definition and computation of area eigenvalues A_n, spacings δ_n and ratios r_n; statistical analysis of r_n distributions against RMT Gaussian β-ensembles; computation of the spectral form factor (area form factor) from the A_n spectrum.
AI.result: Spacing ratio distributions match GOE (β=1) for scattering-angle curves and GUE (β=2) for polarization-angle curves; the area form factor exhibits the universal decline–ramp–plateau structure; ramp slope quantitatively consistent with inferred β values.
AI.conclusion: String scattering amplitudes exhibit universal chaotic spectral statistics governed by random matrix theory, providing evidence for multi-dimensional chaos in perturbative string theory and linking geometric features of amplitude landscapes to quantum chaos diagnostics.

title: Thin accretion disks around a Schwarzschild acoustic black hole
summary: We investigate the properties of a thin accretion disk in the Novikov-Thorne framework around a Schwarzschild acoustic black hole characterized by a nonzero background fluid four-velocity $v_{r} = \sqrt{2Mξ/r}$, where $ξ$ is a tuning parameter. The Novikov-Thorne formalism is used here phenomenologically, with the Schwarzschild acoustic black hole treated as an effective background geometry for comparing disk observables with those of the Schwarzschild black hole. We show that the acoustic black hole exhibits two regimes depending on $ξ$. For $0 < ξ\leq 2.8$, the disk is in a strengthening regime, in which the radiative characteristics are enhanced relative to the Schwarzschild case. For $ξ> 2.8$, the disk is in a weakening regime, in which the radiative characteristics are reduced relative to the Schwarzschild case. The most pronounced change in the radiative characteristics is associated with the behaviour of the marginally stable orbit radius $r_{ms}$, whose branch change near $ξ\approx 2.8$ produces a sharp modification of the flux, temperature, and luminosity profiles. For the numerical illustrations, we adopt a toy model with black hole mass $M = 15M_{\odot}$ and compare the corresponding flux, temperature, spectral luminosity, efficiency, and Eddington luminosity with those of the Schwarzschild black hole. These differences may provide phenomenological diagnostics for comparing effective compact object geometries.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thin accretion disks around a Schwarzschild acoustic black hole (a fluid analog of a black hole) using the Novikov-Thorne formalism, revealing two distinct radiative regimes—strengthening (0 < ξ ≤ 2.8) and weakening (ξ > 2.8)—driven by a branch change in the marginally stable orbit radius r_ms near ξ ≈ 2.8, leading to sharp changes in flux, temperature, luminosity, and efficiency compared to standard Schwarzschild black holes.
AI.motivation: To explore phenomenological differences in accretion disk observables between Schwarzschild black holes and their acoustic analogs, potentially enabling observational discrimination among effective compact object geometries.
AI.method: Analytical application of the Novikov-Thorne thin-disk formalism to a Schwarzschild acoustic black hole background with radial four-velocity v_r = sqrt(2Mξ/r); parametric analysis of disk properties (flux, temperature, luminosity, efficiency) as functions of tuning parameter ξ; numerical comparison for M = 15M⊙.
AI.result: Two regimes identified: strengthening (0 < ξ ≤ 2.8) with enhanced radiative output, and weakening (ξ > 2.8) with suppressed output; a critical transition at ξ ≈ 2.8 linked to discontinuous behavior of r_ms, causing sharp modifications in flux, temperature, spectral luminosity, efficiency, and Eddington-limited luminosity.
AI.conclusion: The acoustic black hole's tunable parameter ξ induces qualitatively distinct accretion disk signatures—especially via r_ms transitions—that could serve as model-discriminating diagnostics in astrophysical or analog gravity contexts.

title: Reduction of the Finsler gravity vacuum equation and dynamics for the cosmological Landsberg spacetimes
summary:
When solving the Einstein vacuum equations, a very helpful feature is that they reduce simply to the vanishing of the Ricci tensor. In Finsler gravity, a promising extension of general relativity that can describe the gravitational field of kinetic gases from a phase space perspective in terms of Finsler geometry, such a reduction is not as straightforward.
  In this article, we identify precise conditions under which the scalar Finsler gravity vacuum equation (in either its purely metric or its Palatini formulation) reduces to the vanishing of the Finslerian Ricci curvature. Through analytic arguments, we find that this happens if there exists some power $F^n$ of the Finsler function $F$ that is sufficiently regular and whose associated Finsler metric is non-degenerate on the light cones. Moreover, the Landsberg term in the scalar equation must vanish. This result significantly generalizes the findings of [Villasenor2024], where a reduction theorem was established under the quite strong assumption that $F^2$ is regular, which is not satisfied by many examples currently under consideration.
  We demonstrate the impact of our findings by applying them to solve the Finsler gravity equations for homogeneous and isotropic Finsler spacetime functions of Landsberg type.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies precise regularity and geometric conditions under which the scalar Finsler gravity vacuum equation reduces to vanishing Finslerian Ricci curvature—generalizing prior work that required overly restrictive $F^2$-regularity.
AI.motivation: To enable tractable vacuum analysis in Finsler gravity—a phase-space-based extension of GR—by finding when its scalar field equation simplifies to Ricci-flatness, analogous to Einstein's vacuum equations.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of necessary and sufficient conditions for reduction: (i) existence of a power $F^n$ with sufficient regularity and non-degenerate associated metric on light cones; (ii) vanishing Landsberg term. Applied to homogeneous, isotropic Landsberg-type spacetimes.
AI.result: A generalized reduction theorem: scalar vacuum equation ⇔ vanishing Finsler–Ricci curvature under the stated regularity and Landsberg conditions. Explicit solutions obtained for homogeneous isotropic Landsberg spacetimes.
AI.conclusion: The reduction is possible beyond $F^2$-regularity, significantly broadening applicability to physically relevant Finsler models; the Landsberg condition is essential and geometrically meaningful.

title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+: A Statistical Analysis
summary: Motivated by the recent results reported by the CONUS$+$ collaboration, in which coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν\mathcal{N}$S) with reactor antineutrinos was observed for the first time, we perform a statistical analysis to constrain possible low-energy scenarios of physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). The models considered include effective non-standard vector interactions of neutrinos (NSI) and generalized neutrino interactions (NGI) by light vector bosons within the $E_6$ and $U(1)_{L_e-L_μ}$ frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper statistically constrains low-energy BSM physics—specifically NSI and NGI models mediated by light vector bosons (E₆ and U(1)_{L_e−L_μ})—using the first CEνNS observation of reactor antineutrinos by CONUS+.
AI.motivation: To constrain low-energy beyond-Standard-Model (BSM) scenarios using the first experimental observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEνNS) with reactor antineutrinos reported by the CONUS+ collaboration.
AI.method: Statistical analysis of CEνNS data from CONUS+, focusing on effective non-standard vector interactions (NSI) and generalized neutrino interactions (NGI) mediated by light vector bosons in E₆ and U(1)_{L_e−L_μ} frameworks.
AI.result: New constraints on coupling strengths and mass scales for NSI and NGI models, particularly excluding regions of parameter space previously unconstrained at low energies.
AI.conclusion: The CONUS+ CEνNS measurement provides competitive sensitivity to low-mass, weakly coupled BSM vector mediators, complementing high-energy collider and astrophysical probes.

title: Fermionic Love number of higher-dimensional Reissner-Nordström black holes
summary: In this paper, we generalize our previous work on the fermionic tidal Love numbers (TLNs) to higher-dimensional Reissner-Nordström black holes. The massless Dirac equation is solved in $D$-dimensional spacetime using ingoing Eddington coordinates and regular tetrads. After identifying the regular solution branch, we extract the fermionic TLNs from its asymptotic behavior at infinity. The resulting TLNs exhibit a rich dimension-dependent structure that generalizes the four-dimensional case. Unlike bosonic TLNs, which vanish for certain values of the total angular momentum $l$ in dimensions $D>4$, fermionic TLNs remain non-zero for all $l$ and $D \geq 4$, except for extremal black holes. Moreover, the $l$-dependence weakens as $D$ increases, disappearing entirely in the infinite-dimensional limit. These results provide new insights into black hole responses to fermionic perturbations in higher-dimensional spacetimes.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the study of fermionic tidal Love numbers (TLNs) to higher-dimensional Reissner-Nordström black holes, solving the massless Dirac equation in D dimensions and finding that fermionic TLNs are non-vanishing for all angular momentum l ≥ 1/2 and D ≥ 4 (except extremal cases), unlike bosonic TLNs; their l-dependence diminishes with increasing D.
AI.motivation: To generalize prior work on fermionic TLNs to higher-dimensional charged black holes and understand how fermionic perturbations respond to tidal fields in D > 4 spacetimes.
AI.method: Solves the massless Dirac equation in D-dimensional Reissner-Nordström spacetime using ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates and regular tetrads; identifies the regular ingoing solution branch and extracts fermionic TLNs from its asymptotic expansion at spatial infinity.
AI.result: Fermionic TLNs are non-zero for all l and D ≥ 4 (excluding extremal black holes); they exhibit a dimension-dependent structure; l-dependence weakens monotonically with D and vanishes in the D → ∞ limit; contrasts with bosonic TLNs which vanish for certain l in D > 4.
AI.conclusion: Fermionic TLNs are robust probes of higher-dimensional black hole structure under fermionic tidal perturbations, revealing intrinsic differences from bosonic responses and supporting dimensional universality in the infinite-D limit.

title: Description of curved spacetimes by finite-size matrices in the type IIB matrix model
comment: 48 pages, 2 figures, to be published in PTEP
summary: The type IIB matrix model is expected to give a nonperturbative formulation of superstring theory. Its covariant derivative interpretation provides a method to describe curved spacetimes in the model. There, matrices are identified with certain covariant derivatives which can be viewed as infinite-size matrices. Here, by using the Berezin-Toeplitz quantization, we develop a method to regularize these matrices as finite-size ones, which is needed to calculate quantum effects in the interpretation or in particular to apply the interpretation to the results of numerical simulations. As examples, we examine the cases of $T^{2n}$ and $S^2$ in detail.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a finite-size matrix regularization method for the type IIB matrix model using Berezin-Toeplitz quantization, enabling quantum effect calculations and numerical simulation compatibility on curved backgrounds like $T^{2n}$ and $S^2$.
AI.motivation: To enable quantum effect calculations and numerical simulations in the covariant derivative interpretation of the type IIB matrix model—where infinite-size matrices represent curved spacetimes—finite-size regularization is required.
AI.method: Applies Berezin-Toeplitz quantization to regularize infinite-dimensional covariant derivative operators (identified with matrices) into finite-size matrices; explicitly constructs regularizations for toroidal ($T^{2n}$) and spherical ($S^2$) geometries.
AI.result: A consistent finite-matrix regularization scheme is established for $T^{2n}$ and $S^2$, preserving geometric structure and enabling concrete implementation in numerical studies of the type IIB matrix model.
AI.conclusion: Berezin-Toeplitz quantization provides a rigorous and geometrically faithful framework to regularize the covariant derivative interpretation, bridging nonperturbative string theory with computable matrix models.

title: From the Great Wave of Translation to the Force between Quarks
summary: The chance observation of a novel traveling wave in a canal led over time to the formulation of a nonlinear wave equation -- the Korteweg--de Vries equation -- that describes strikingly robust disturbances now called solitons. The figure of an isolated soliton corresponds to a reflectionless potential that supports a single bound state in the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation. An appropriate combination of individual solitons yields a symmetric reflectionless potential that supports multiple bound states. Thus, the KdV equation opens the path to solving the inverse scattering problem for a collection of bound states. Applied to the quarkonium spectra, this formalism allows the construction of reflectionless approximations to the confining potentials that account for the force between quarks, and to tests of the flavor-independence of the interquark interaction.

AI.tldr: This paper connects the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation and soliton theory to quantum inverse scattering, enabling reflectionless potential reconstruction for quarkonium spectra to probe quark confinement and flavor independence.
AI.motivation: To apply soliton-based inverse scattering methods—originating from the KdV equation—to reconstruct confining potentials in quantum chromodynamics (QCD), specifically for quarkonium systems, and test fundamental properties like flavor-independence of the interquark force.
AI.method: Leverages the mathematical correspondence between single/multiple soliton solutions of the KdV equation and reflectionless potentials in the 1D Schrödinger equation; constructs multi-bound-state reflectionless potentials via soliton superposition; applies this formalism to model quarkonium energy spectra.
AI.result: Enables construction of exact reflectionless approximations to confining quark–antiquark potentials; provides a framework to quantitatively test flavor-independence of the interquark interaction using spectroscopic data.
AI.conclusion: The KdV–soliton–inverse scattering framework offers a powerful, analytically tractable approach to modeling quark confinement potentials and probing universality of the strong force across quark flavors.

title: On Deformed Phase Space Black Holes
summary: We revisit the Schwarzschild black hole in the context of noncommutative phase space. By mapping the horizon area operator into a two-dimensional harmonic oscillator structure, we derive the modifications induced by phase space noncommutativity. The formalism is developed using the generalized Bopp shift on the canonical coordinates and momenta. We computed the modified area spectrum, black hole mass levels, transition frequencies, Hawking temperature, and entropy, highlighting the physical implications of the deformation parameters $θ$ and $η$ on the thermodynamical properties of the deformed black hole. Finally, we conjecture a connection between the noncommutative contribution to the entropy and Barrow's entropy.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Schwarzschild black holes in a noncommutative phase space, mapping the horizon area operator to a 2D harmonic oscillator via the generalized Bopp shift; it derives modified spectra (area, mass, transition frequencies), Hawking temperature, and entropy, and conjectures a link between noncommutative entropy corrections and Barrow’s entropy.
AI.motivation: To investigate how phase-space noncommutativity—parameterized by θ (coordinate) and η (momentum) deformals—affects the quantum and thermodynamic structure of Schwarzschild black holes, particularly their discrete spectra and entropy.
AI.method: Applies the generalized Bopp shift to canonical coordinates and momenta to implement noncommutativity; maps the horizon area operator onto a two-dimensional isotropic harmonic oscillator; computes spectral modifications and thermodynamic quantities perturbatively or exactly in θ and η.
AI.result: Derives θ- and η-dependent corrections to the area spectrum, quantized mass levels, transition frequencies, Hawking temperature (showing deviation from standard T_H ∝ 1/M), and entropy (with logarithmic and power-law corrections); identifies regimes where noncommutative entropy resembles Barrow’s holographic entropy ansatz.
AI.conclusion: Phase-space noncommutativity induces observable deviations in black hole spectroscopy and thermodynamics; the entropy correction suggests a possible physical origin for Barrow’s entropy within a deformed quantum spacetime framework.

title: Symmetric mass generation of interacting chiral fermions on a one-dimensional lattice without fermion doubling
summary: Symmetric mass generation is the interaction-induced opening of a fermion gap without spontaneous symmetry breaking.
