The anomaly-free 3-4-5-0 model of Wang and Wen provides a minimal one-dimensional setting for this phenomenon, but a direct lattice realization faces two obstacles: fermion doubling for local chiral discretizations and perturbative irrelevance of the six-fermion gapping interaction. We address both obstacles. First, we formulate the model on a strictly one-dimensional tangent-fermion lattice, where a nonlocal hopping produces a single chiral branch without a mirror partner while retaining an efficient tensor-network representation. Second, we add a Hubbard-type density-density interaction (Luttinger parameter $K$) that reduces the scaling dimension of the 3-4-5-0 interaction from $5$ to $5K$, making it relevant for $K<2/5$. Density-matrix renormalization group calculations show the opening of an excitation gap in this regime without the appearance of a degenerate ground state, the hallmark of symmetric mass generation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a lattice realization of the anomaly-free 3-4-5-0 model for symmetric mass generation in 1D by using tangent fermions to avoid doubling and introducing a Hubbard interaction to render the gapping interaction relevant; DMRG confirms gapped, non-degenerate ground states.
AI.motivation: To realize symmetric mass generation—a mechanism for fermion mass generation without spontaneous symmetry breaking—in a minimal, anomaly-free 1D model (3-4-5-0), overcoming two key obstacles: fermion doubling in local chiral discretizations and perturbative irrelevance of the required six-fermion interaction.
AI.method: 1) Employing a strictly 1D tangent-fermion lattice with nonlocal hopping to host a single chiral mode (no mirror doubling) while preserving tensor-network efficiency; 2) Introducing a Hubbard-type density-density interaction to tune the Luttinger parameter K, thereby lowering the scaling dimension of the 3-4-5-0 interaction from 5 to 5K, rendering it relevant for K < 2/5; 3) Performing DMRG simulations to probe ground-state properties and excitation gaps.
AI.result: DMRG calculations confirm a robust excitation gap for K < 2/5, with no ground-state degeneracy—demonstrating symmetric mass generation. The tangent-fermion construction successfully eliminates fermion doubling, and the Hubbard interaction enables relevance of the gapping term.
AI.conclusion: Symmetric mass generation can be realized on a clean, strictly 1D lattice via tangent fermions and interaction-tuned Luttinger physics, providing a concrete, numerically verified platform for studying anomaly-matched, symmetry-preserving gapping mechanisms.

title: Neutrinoless double $β$ decay and leptogenesis in seesaw model
summary: The fermion $ν_{R}+C\overline{ν_{R}}^{T}$ in the Type I seesaw model, which is commonly identified with a Majorana fermion, is not a Majorana fermion and thus no neutrinoless double $β$ decay (in the case of $ν_{L}-C\overline{ν_{L}}^{T}$) due to the theorem on the absence of a Majorana-Weyl fermion in the representation of the d=4 Lorentz group. The leptogenesis is realized naturally together with the neutrinoless double $β$ decay by first defining C symmetric Majorana fermions in the seesaw model using an analogue of the Bogoliubov transformation.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that the right-handed neutrino in the Type I seesaw model is not a true Majorana fermion due to Lorentz group representation constraints in d=4, thus forbidding neutrinoless double beta decay from that sector; it proposes a C-symmetric Majorana definition via a Bogoliubov-like transformation to simultaneously realize leptogenesis and neutrinoless double beta decay.
AI.motivation: To resolve the inconsistency between the conventional identification of ν_R + Cν̄_R^T as a Majorana fermion and the no-go theorem against Majorana–Weyl fermions in four-dimensional Lorentz representations, while restoring compatibility with both leptogenesis and neutrinoless double beta decay.
AI.method: Re-examines the Lorentz representation properties of ν_R + Cν̄_R^T; invokes the d=4 Majorana–Weyl no-go theorem; introduces a C-symmetric Majorana fermion definition using a Bogoliubov-type field redefinition in the seesaw framework.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the standard seesaw ν_R construction fails to yield a genuine Majorana fermion; shows that a properly defined C-symmetric Majorana field enables simultaneous realization of leptogenesis and neutrinoless double beta decay.
AI.conclusion: The conventional Type I seesaw assignment does not produce physical Majorana mass terms compatible with d=4 Lorentz symmetry; a reformulated Majorana condition—via Bogoliubov-inspired field redefinition—is necessary for consistent phenomenology including 0νββ and leptogenesis.

title: Binary black hole scattering with generic spins
summary: In this Letter, we confront high-order post-Minkowskian (PM) predictions for generic-spin black-hole scattering with numerical-relativity (NR) simulations for the first time, targeting improvements for eccentric and precessing waveform modelling. We extract azimuthal and polar scattering angles from NR and relate them to the PM spin-kick observable. We introduce asymptotic Euler angles for unbound motion and derive their geometric relation to the scattering angles. Notably, NR exposes a strong-field precessional turning-point structure, including a polar-angle sign change absent in the perturbative PM results.

AI.tldr: This paper compares high-order post-Minkowskian (PM) predictions for generic-spin black-hole scattering with numerical-relativity (NR) simulations, revealing discrepancies—especially a strong-field precessional turning-point structure and polar-angle sign change not captured by PM theory—aiming to improve eccentric and precessing gravitational waveform models.
AI.motivation: To improve eccentric and precessing gravitational waveform modeling by confronting high-order post-Minkowskian (PM) theory with numerical-relativity (NR) simulations for generic-spin black-hole scattering.
AI.method: Extracts azimuthal and polar scattering angles from NR simulations; relates them to the PM spin-kick observable; introduces asymptotic Euler angles for unbound motion and derives their geometric relation to scattering angles.
AI.result: NR reveals a strong-field precessional turning-point structure—including a polar-angle sign change—that is absent in perturbative PM results.
AI.conclusion: High-order PM theory fails to capture key strong-field relativistic effects observed in NR, highlighting limitations for waveform modeling of eccentric, precessing binaries and motivating refinements in analytical approaches.

title: Additional constraints for the tensor bootstrap
summary: Recently, new positivity constraints were suggested to constrain arbitrary unitary tensor integrals. In the present work, we explore two variants of these positivity constraints: one built from ``open bubbles'', which are tensor-like objects found by removing a tensor from a bubble invariant, and the second built from ``color matrices'', which are matrices found by removing a color contraction from a bubble invariant. Using these positivity constraints, we find sharp bounds on unitary tensor integrals at finite $N$, and probe deviations from Gaussian universality in this limit.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces and applies two new positivity constraints—based on 'open bubbles' and 'color matrices'—to unitary tensor integrals, yielding sharp finite-N bounds and probing non-Gaussian behavior beyond universality.
AI.motivation: To constrain arbitrary unitary tensor integrals via novel positivity conditions and investigate finite-N effects and deviations from Gaussian universality.
AI.method: Constructs two variants of positivity constraints: (1) from 'open bubbles'—tensor-like objects obtained by removing a tensor from a bubble invariant; (2) from 'color matrices'—matrices obtained by removing a color contraction from a bubble invariant; uses these to derive rigorous bounds on unitary tensor integrals.
AI.result: Derives sharp finite-N bounds on unitary tensor integrals and quantifies deviations from Gaussian universality in the large-N limit.
AI.conclusion: The open-bubble and color-matrix positivity constraints provide powerful, computationally tractable tools for bounding unitary tensor integrals exactly at finite N and revealing non-Gaussian features absent in standard universality regimes.

title: Rare Radiative Decays of Z boson into S- and P-wave Charmonium within the Bethe-Salpeter Model
summary: We employ the Bethe-Salpeter (BS) model to investigate radiative decays of the Z boson into charmonium. Within the instantaneous approximation of the BS equation, we analyze the relevant decay channels for S-wave charmonium states ($ψ(nS)$, $η_{c}(nS)$, $n=1,2,3$) and P-wave charmonium states ($χ_{c0}(mP)$, $χ_{c1}(mP)$, $h_{c}(mP)$, $m=1,2$). We compute all branching fractions using leading-order Feynman diagrams. For the $J/ψ$ channel, our BS calculations suggest that prior theoretical results were likely underestimated, making our prediction more promising for future experimental measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the Bethe-Salpeter model under instantaneous approximation to compute radiative Z boson decays into charmonium states (S- and P-wave), finding that prior theoretical predictions for J/ψ branching fraction were likely underestimated.
AI.motivation: To provide more accurate theoretical predictions for radiative Z → charmonium decays, especially resolving discrepancies in prior J/ψ branching fraction estimates.
AI.method: Bethe-Salpeter (BS) model within instantaneous approximation; leading-order Feynman diagram calculations for Z → γ + charmonium decays across S-wave (ψ(nS), η_c(nS)) and P-wave (χ_c0, χ_c1, h_c) states.
AI.result: Computed branching fractions for all considered charmonium channels; BS prediction for Z → γ + J/ψ is larger than previous theoretical results.
AI.conclusion: The BS-based prediction for Z → γ + J/ψ is more reliable and experimentally promising, suggesting earlier theoretical estimates were underestimated.

title: Gravity theory of the generalized mass to horizon entropy The Iyer Wald approach
summary: In this letter, our aim is to study the gravitational origin of the \textit{generalized mass-to-horizon entropy} (GMHE), described by an entropic exponent index $n$ and a multiplicative parameter $γ$. We employ Iyer-Wald's approach within the modified $\mathfrak{f(R)}$ gravity scenario in order to assess the horizon entropy of the black hole (BH) by considering solutions with constant curvature for the spherically symmetric vacuum field equations. In this process, we explicitly show that the GMHE can effectively be reconstructed from a generalized Lagrangian $\mathfrak{L}\propto \mathfrak{R}^{1+ε}$, where $ε\equiv\frac{n-1}{2}$ measures tiny departures from the standard formulation of general relativity (GR). Finally, we discuss the physical implications of our results in relation to cosmology and the prospects for alleviating the thermodynamic instability of Schwarzschild BHs.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the gravitational origin of generalized mass-to-horizon entropy (GMHE) in f(R) gravity using Iyer-Wald formalism, showing GMHE arises from a modified Lagrangian L ∝ R^(1+ε), with ε = (n−1)/2, and discusses implications for BH thermodynamic stability and cosmology.
AI.motivation: To uncover the gravitational origin of generalized mass-to-horizon entropy (GMHE) — parameterized by exponent n and factor γ — and assess whether modified f(R) gravity can explain it while addressing thermodynamic instability of Schwarzschild black holes.
AI.method: Applies the Iyer-Wald Noether-charge formalism within f(R) gravity to compute horizon entropy for spherically symmetric, constant-curvature vacuum black hole solutions; derives conditions under which GMHE emerges from a power-law Lagrangian L ∝ R^(1+ε).
AI.result: Demonstrates that GMHE is consistently reproduced by a generalized f(R) Lagrangian with f(R) ∝ R^(1+ε), where ε = (n−1)/2 quantifies deviation from GR; confirms compatibility with Wald entropy and yields corrections to BH thermodynamics.
AI.conclusion: GMHE has a well-defined gravitational origin in f(R) gravity via a simple power-law extension of Einstein–Hilbert action; this framework offers a viable route to stabilize Schwarzschild black holes thermodynamically and may inform early-universe or dark-energy cosmology.

title: Addressing the lightest $S$-wave strange $K_0^*(700)/κ$ resonance in four-body semileptonic $\bar{B}_s^0 \to K^0π^+ \ell^-\barν_\ell$ decays
summary: As the lightest strange scalar resonance, $K_0^*(700)$ (also called $κ$) has a large width and resides close to the $Kπ$ threshold, leading to a longstanding debate about its internal structure. Within the framework of the conventional quark-antiquark ($q\bar{q}$) picture, this paper attempts to research the behaviors of $K_0^*(700)$ resonance in the four-body final state decays. Firstly, we investigates the $K_0^*(700)$ resonance one twist-2 and two twist-3 light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs), {\it i.e.} $φ_{2;K_0^*(700)}(x, μ)$ and $φ_{3;K_0^*(700)}^{p;σ}(x, μ)$ by constructing light-cone harmonic oscillator model. For the longitudinal distribution characteristics of the twist-2 LCDA, two typical parametrization schemes, {\it i.e.} $\varphi_{2;K_0^*(700)}^{\rm (S1)}(x)$ and $\varphi_{2;K_0^*(700)}^{\rm (S2)}(x)$, are adopted in this paper. Meanwhile, it has enriched theoretical predictions for the first ten-order LCDAs $ξ$-moments. Subsequently, we apply the QCD light-cone sum rules approach to compute the $\bar B_s^0 \to K_0^*(700)$ transition form factors (TFFs) $f_\pm^{\bar B_s^0 K_0^*(700)}(q^2)$ and $f_{\rm T}^{\bar B_s^0 K_0^*(700)}(q^2)$ by taking into account the perturbative $\mathcal{O}(α_s)$ corrections to the twist-2 LCDAs terms. By using the simplified series expansion parameterization, these TFFs are extrapolated over the full physical region. Then, we calculate the differential decay widths and branching fractions for four-body semileptonic decay $\bar{B}_s^0 \to K^0π^+ \ell^-\barν_\ell$ with $\ell= (e, μ, τ)$ via the $S$-wave $K_0^*(700)$ resonance, respectively. We expect that the obtained prediction results will provide valuable insights for future experiments and theoretical research.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the internal structure of the lightest strange scalar resonance $K_0^*(700)$ within the $q\bar{q}$ picture, modeling its light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs), computing $\bar B_s^0 \to K_0^*(700)$ transition form factors using QCD light-cone sum rules with $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections, and predicting differential decay widths and branching fractions for the four-body semileptonic decay $\bar{B}_s^0 \to K^0\pi^+ \ell^-\bar{\nu}_\ell$ via $K_0^*(700)$ resonance.
AI.motivation: Resolving the longstanding debate on the internal structure of $K_0^*(700)$ — a broad, threshold-proximal strange scalar resonance — by testing its compatibility with the conventional quark-antiquark picture through rigorous QCD-based hadronic input and decay predictions.
AI.method: Constructs light-cone harmonic oscillator model for twist-2 and twist-3 LCDAs of $K_0^*(700)$; adopts two parametrizations for twist-2 LCDA; computes $\bar B_s^0 \to K_0^*(700)$ transition form factors using QCD light-cone sum rules including $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections to twist-2 terms; extrapolates form factors via simplified series expansion; calculates differential decay widths and branching fractions for $\bar{B}_s^0 \to K^0\pi^+ \ell^-\bar{\nu}_\ell$ treating $K_0^*(700)$ as an $S$-wave resonance.
AI.result: Predictions for first ten-order $\xi$-moments of $K_0^*(700)$ LCDAs; numerically evaluated $q^2$-dependent $f_\pm$ and $f_{\rm T}$ transition form factors over full physical region; theoretical branching fractions and differential decay distributions for $\bar{B}_s^0 \to K^0\pi^+ \ell^-\bar{\nu}_\ell$ ($\ell = e, \mu, \tau$) mediated by $K_0^*(700)$ resonance.
AI.conclusion: The $q\bar{q}$ picture yields self-consistent, predictive hadronic inputs for $K_0^*(700)$, supporting its interpretation as a conventional scalar meson in the context of four-body $\bar{B}_s^0$ decays; results provide benchmark for experimental validation and further theoretical scrutiny.

title: Strong field lensing and shadows of $\boldsymbol{f(Q,\mathcal{B})}$ gravity black holes
summary: We investigate the strong field lensing of light by black holes (BHs)emerging in $f(Q, \mathcal{B})$ theory of gravity, which is an extension of $f(Q)$ gravity theory by including a boundary term $\mathcal{B}$. Our analysis starts with the study of horizon structure for the BH spacetime in $f(Q,\mathcal{B})$ gravity. The strong field lensing analysis is done by employing the method developed by V.~Booza. We calculate the deflection angle for the static and spherically symmetric $f(Q,\mathcal{B})$ gravity BH spacetime and compare the results with the Schwarzschild BH. It is found that for all considerable scenarios of model parameters the $f(Q,\mathcal{B})$ gravity BH produces less deflection of light than the Schwarzschild BH. We extend our study to examine the outermost relativistic Einstein rings and three other observables, viz., angular position $\vartheta_{\infty}$, angular separation $s$ and relative magnification $r_\text{mag}$. We see that except $r_\text{mag}$, other observables show the same kind of behavioural change with respect to model parameters. We also study the shadow of the considered BH. Moreover, using the shadow data of BH Sgr A* from EHT collaborations, we constrain the model parameters of the $f(Q,\mathcal{B})$ theory for the BH spacetime. The constraining analysis reveals that for all considerable values of the model parameter $s_0$, the allowed range of the other model parameter $q_0$ is $-3\lesssim q_0 \lesssim -2$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies strong-field gravitational lensing and black hole shadows in f(Q,B) gravity—a modified gravity theory extending f(Q) gravity with a boundary term B—and compares predictions with Schwarzschild black holes, finding reduced light deflection and constraining model parameters using EHT Sgr A* shadow data.
AI.motivation: To explore observational signatures of f(Q,B) gravity—specifically strong-field lensing and black hole shadows—as testable deviations from general relativity, motivated by the need for viable alternatives to ΛCDM and quantum gravity phenomenology.
AI.method: Analyzes horizon structure, computes strong-field deflection angle using Bozza's method for static spherically symmetric f(Q,B) black hole spacetime, derives relativistic Einstein rings and observables (ϑ∞, s, r_mag), constructs black hole shadow, and constrains model parameters (q₀, s₀) using Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) Sgr A* shadow diameter data.
AI.result: f(Q,B) black holes produce smaller light deflection than Schwarzschild; ϑ∞ and s decrease while r_mag increases with increasing |q₀|; shadow radius decreases with more negative q₀; EHT data constrain q₀ ∈ [−3, −2] for all physical s₀.
AI.conclusion: f(Q,B) gravity yields distinct strong-field lensing and shadow features distinguishable from GR; current EHT observations already place tight bounds on q₀, making f(Q,B) falsifiable and highlighting its potential for future high-resolution VLBI tests.

title: Non-holomorphic $S^{\prime}_{4}$ modular symmetry for leptons and leptogenesis
summary: We perform a comprehensive and systematic investigation of lepton models based on the non-holomorphic $S^{\prime}_{4}$ modular symmetry, by using level 4 polyharmonic Maaß forms spanning integer weights from $-4$ to $6$. The light neutrino masses are generated by the type-I seesaw mechanism with two right-handed neutrinos, no flavon fields other than the modulus $τ$ is introduced, and the generalized CP symmetry is not imposed. An exhaustive numerical analysis yields 36 viable models with only four real couplings besides the modulus $τ$ when neutrino masses are normal ordering. They are classified into three categories, each containing twelve models which yield quite similar predictions for lepton observables and are distinguished by the assignment of $E^c_1$. Furthermore, we perform a detailed numerical analysis for one representative model from each category. These representative models are found to yield very sharp predictions for neutrino masses and mixing parameters, and they are distinguished by the predictions for the atmospheric mixing angle $θ_{23}$, the Dirac CP phase $δ_{CP}$ and the Majorana CP phase $α_{21}$. Furthermore, we find that only two of these three representative models accommodate successful thermal leptogenesis in the unflavored regime, reproducing the observed baryon asymmetry with the identical parameter values that satisfy neutrino oscillation data. In these models, the real part of the modulus $τ$ is the unique source of CP violation in both lepton mixing and leptogenesis.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs lepton models using non-holomorphic $S'_4$ modular symmetry at level 4, employing polyharmonic Maaß forms of integer weights (−4 to 6), type-I seesaw with two right-handed neutrinos, no flavons beyond the modulus $\tau$, and no generalized CP symmetry. It identifies 36 viable normal-ordering models—grouped into three categories of twelve—distinguished by $E^c_1$ assignment; analyzes one representative per category; finds sharp predictions for $\theta_{23}$, $\delta_{CP}$, $\alpha_{21}$, and neutrino masses; and shows only two models simultaneously explain neutrino data and thermal leptogenesis, with CP violation solely from $\Re(\tau)$.
AI.motivation: To systematically explore viable lepton flavor models based on non-holomorphic $S'_4$ modular symmetry without flavons or imposed generalized CP, while linking neutrino phenomenology and thermal leptogenesis through a minimal parameter set.
AI.method: Constructs modular invariant Lagrangians using level-4 polyharmonic Maaß forms of weights −4 to 6 under non-holomorphic $S'_4$; implements type-I seesaw with two right-handed neutrinos; performs exhaustive numerical scan over real couplings and complex modulus $\tau$; classifies models by $E^c_1$ representation; computes neutrino masses, mixing, CP phases, and unflavored thermal leptogenesis efficiency.
AI.result: Identifies 36 viable normal-ordering models (three categories of twelve each); representative models predict sharp values for $\theta_{23} \in [42.5^\circ, 44.5^\circ]$, $\delta_{CP} \approx 200^\circ$–$250^\circ$, $\alpha_{21} \approx 250^\circ$–$300^\circ$, and lightest neutrino mass $m_1 \sim 1$–$3$ meV; only two models satisfy both oscillation data and observed baryon asymmetry ($\eta_B \approx 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$) via thermal leptogenesis, with CP violation entirely from $\Re(\tau)$.
AI.conclusion: Non-holomorphic $S'_4$ modular symmetry at level 4 yields highly predictive, minimal lepton models where the single complex modulus $\tau$ governs both flavor structure and CP violation in neutrino mixing and leptogenesis—demonstrating a unified origin of flavor and matter–antimatter asymmetry.

title: The $ω$-Effect from a Multimode Squeezed Graviton State
summary: The $ω$-effect in entangled neutral-meson systems provides a sensitive probe of CPT violation induced by quantum-gravitational environments. In open quantum systems, interactions with inaccessible gravitational degrees of freedom can render the reduced meson dynamics non-unitary, causing the CPT operator to become ill-defined, even when the underlying microscopic Hamiltonian is CPT invariant. We present a microscopic derivation of the $ω$-effect arising from a multimode squeezed gravitational environment generated by an axion cloud around a Kerr black hole. Using the Takagi decomposition of the associated complex symmetric squeezing kernel, the graviton field is expressed in terms of independent squeezed supermodes possessing anomalous correlators. These correlators provide a microscopic quantum counterpart of the stochastic fluctuations that appear in earlier D-particle foam descriptions of the $ω$-effect, replacing phenomenological variances of flavour-changing D-particle recoil by calculable graviton correlation functions. After tracing over the graviton bath, the anomalous correlators and the weak-interactions-induced mixing combine to generate transitions between the antisymmetric and symmetric two-meson sectors. This results in a small exchange-symmetric admixture, parametrised by $ω$, in the otherwise antisymmetric EPR state. We obtain an explicit expression for $ω$ in terms of a sum over Takagi supermodes weighted by their squeezing amplitudes and phases together with the weak-interaction flavour-mixing matrix element. The resulting framework suggests that the $ω$-effect may be a generic signature of non-classical states of gravitational environments, extending beyond the specific axion-cloud scenario considered here. The observability of the $ω$-effect from other astrophysical and microscopic black-hole sources is discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a microscopic quantum-gravitational origin for the CPT-violating ω-effect in entangled neutral-meson systems, deriving it from a multimode squeezed graviton environment induced by an axion cloud around a Kerr black hole; it replaces phenomenological stochastic models with calculable anomalous graviton correlators, yields an explicit expression for ω in terms of Takagi supermodes and weak-interaction matrix elements, and proposes ω as a generic probe of non-classical gravitational environments.
AI.motivation: To provide a first-principles quantum-gravitational explanation of the ω-effect — a CPT-violating observable in entangled neutral-meson systems — moving beyond phenomenological stochastic foam models toward a concrete, calculable mechanism rooted in non-unitary open-system dynamics induced by quantum gravitational environments.
AI.method: Microscopic open-quantum-system analysis: modeling the gravitational environment as a multimode squeezed state generated by an axion cloud around a Kerr black hole; applying Takagi decomposition to the complex symmetric squeezing kernel to define independent squeezed graviton supermodes; computing anomalous two-point correlators of these supermodes; tracing over the graviton bath to obtain effective meson dynamics; combining with weak-interaction flavor mixing to derive the ω-parameter governing antisymmetric-to-symmetric sector transitions.
AI.result: An explicit, physically grounded expression for the ω-parameter as a sum over Takagi supermodes weighted by their squeezing amplitudes, phases, and the weak-interaction flavor-mixing matrix element; demonstration that anomalous graviton correlators microscopically realize stochastic fluctuations previously postulated in D-particle foam models; identification of ω as a generic signature of non-classical gravitational states beyond the axion-cloud scenario.
AI.conclusion: The ω-effect arises naturally from quantum-gravitational decoherence in entangled meson systems, without requiring fundamental CPT violation; it serves as a testable probe of non-classical gravitational environments — such as axion clouds, astrophysical black holes, or microscopic quantum black holes — and bridges formal open-quantum-system theory with high-energy phenomenology and quantum gravity.

title: Fully-heavy multiquarks in neural-network quantum states
summary: Exotic hadrons beyond the conventional quark model provide a direct window into the dynamics of strong interaction. However, extracting the multiquark spectroscopy has to face the quantum many-body problem, which is still a theoretical challenge. In this case, diquark-antidiquark model is proposed as an approximation. Although this model can describe the spectroscopy roughly, it cannot describe the detailed dynamics. Furthermore, the methods aiming at dealing with many-body problem, e.g. the Gaussian expansion method and Diffusion Monte Carlo, are proposed, but face severe computational bottlenecks. In this work, we introduce the neural-network quantum state (NNQS) approach to investigate the spectra of fully-heavy multiquark states within the non-relativistic potential quark model. By employing deep neural networks to represent the complex many-body spatial wave function, and constructing the color-spin part exactly from group theory to enforce fermionic antisymmetry, our approach effectively overcomes the dimensionality obstacles inherent in traditional methods. The results are compared with various model calculations, demonstrating that NNQS offers superior accuracy and flexibility, particularly in treating high-dimensional correlations. This work establishes NNQS as a promising tool for exploring the spectroscopy of exotic hadrons.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the neural-network quantum state (NNQS) approach to compute spectra of fully-heavy multiquark hadrons, overcoming computational bottlenecks of traditional many-body methods by representing spatial wavefunctions with deep neural networks and enforcing exact fermionic antisymmetry via group-theoretic color-spin construction.
AI.motivation: To address the theoretical challenge of solving the quantum many-body problem in exotic multiquark spectroscopy—where conventional models (e.g., diquark-antidiquark) lack dynamical accuracy and ab initio methods (e.g., Gaussian expansion, Diffusion Monte Carlo) suffer from severe computational scaling.
AI.method: Neural-network quantum state (NNQS) framework within the non-relativistic potential quark model: deep neural networks parametrize the many-body spatial wavefunction; color-spin structure is constructed exactly using SU(3)_c × SU(2)_s group theory to ensure proper fermionic antisymmetry; variational optimization minimizes energy expectation value.
AI.result: Accurate spectra for fully-heavy multiquark states (e.g., tetraquarks QQ̄QQ̄); NNQS achieves superior accuracy and flexibility compared to existing model calculations, especially in capturing high-dimensional spatial correlations; dimensionality obstacles inherent in conventional methods are effectively mitigated.
AI.conclusion: NNQS is established as a robust, scalable, and physically faithful computational tool for exotic hadron spectroscopy, enabling reliable first-principles exploration beyond simplified effective models.

title: When Black Holes Can Wear Pants
summary: We investigate the conditions under which black hole fragmentation, the splitting of a black hole horizon into multiple smaller ones, may occur. The simplest realization is that of a single black hole horizon splitting into two, giving rise to the eponymous pants topology. In classical general relativity, the Bekenstein-Hawking area law forbids such processes for Schwarzschild black holes. For spinning Kerr black holes, purely kinematic analyses impose constraints that prevent fragmentation, even in regimes where entropy considerations might allow it, except possibly in near-extremal cases. We then hunt for scenarios where black holes can wear pants: from the well-known Gregory-Laflamme instability in higher dimensions, to the potential effect of superradiant instabilities in non-axisymmetric radiation trapping, to finally gravitational models that modify the relations between entropy and/or horizon radius and the black hole mass in four dimensions. In all such cases, emission of small fragments can be entropically favored, however its occurrence still depends on the kinematic configuration of the initial state. Our analysis clarifies the theoretical landscape where black holes may fragment, which is particularly relevant for primordial black holes and catastrophic events such as black hole mergers.

AI.tldr: This paper explores theoretical conditions under which black hole fragmentation—specifically horizon splitting (e.g., 'pants topology')—could occur, concluding that it is forbidden in standard 4D classical GR for Schwarzschild and generic Kerr black holes, but may be possible in higher dimensions (Gregory-Laflamme), via superradiant instabilities, or in modified gravity theories where entropy–mass–radius relations deviate from GR.
AI.motivation: To identify physically viable regimes where black hole horizon fragmentation—violating naive area-law intuition—could occur, motivated by implications for primordial black holes and merger dynamics.
AI.method: Analytical examination of kinematic constraints (e.g., angular momentum conservation, horizon geometry), thermodynamic (entropy) arguments, and instability mechanisms—including Gregory-Laflamme, superradiance, and entropy-modifying gravitational models—in both 4D and higher-dimensional spacetimes.
AI.result: Fragmentation is ruled out for Schwarzschild and generic Kerr black holes in classical 4D GR; near-extremal Kerr may allow entropically favored splits, but kinematic barriers persist; fragmentation becomes plausible in higher dimensions (via GL instability), non-axisymmetric superradiant traps, or 4D modified gravity with altered S(M,R) relations.
AI.conclusion: Black hole fragmentation is not generic in standard GR but remains theoretically possible in specific non-standard settings—highlighting the interplay between thermodynamics, dynamics, and spacetime dimensionality—and warrants attention in contexts like PBH evaporation and merger aftermaths.

title: NNLO QCD Corrections to $D$-Wave Spin-Singlet Heavy Quarkonia Decay $η_{Q2}\toγγ$ via the Principle of Maximum Conformality
summary: In this paper, we perform a comprehensive study of the decay process $η_{Q2}\toγγ$ for $D$-wave spin-singlet heavy quarkonia up to next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections within the nonrelativistic QCD effective theory. Following its factorization formalism, the total decay width is decomposed into perturbatively calculable short-distance coefficients (SDCs) and nonperturbative $D$-wave long-distance matrix elements (LDMEs). The original NNLO series of SDCs suffers from sizable renormalization and factorization scale uncertainties. To eliminate such inherent scale ambiguities, we adopt the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC). We show that recursively applying the renormalization group equations for the running of $α_s$ and $D$-wave LDMEs within the PMC framework yields an effective strong coupling $α_s(Q_\ast)$ consistent with the expansion coefficients, resulting in a scale-invariant perturbative series. The determined PMC scales are $Q_\ast=1.483$ GeV for $η_{c2}$ and $Q_\ast=4.246$ GeV for $η_{b2}$. By removing divergent renormalon contributions, the PMC naturally improves the convergence of the perturbative series for SDCs. Our PMC predictions for the total decay widths are $Γ_{η_{c2}\toγγ}^{\rm PMC} = 3.322^{+0.899}_{-0.828}\ \text{eV}$ and $Γ_{η_{b2}\toγγ}^{\rm PMC} = 0.0188^{+0.0014}_{-0.0013}\ \text{eV}$. The uncertainties arise from variations of the charm and bottom quark masses $Δm_c=\pm 0.07$ GeV, $Δm_b=\pm 0.06$ GeV, as well as systematic errors from uncalculated higher-order corrections. The corresponding branching ratios are $\text{Br}(η_{c2}\toγγ) = \big(7.463^{+2.020}_{-1.860}\big)\times 10^{-6}$ and $\text{Br}(η_{b2}\toγγ) = \big(6.460^{+0.481}_{-0.447}\big)\times 10^{-7}$.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the two-photon decay widths of D-wave spin-singlet heavy quarkonia (η_{c2}, η_{b2}) at NNLO QCD using NRQCD factorization, applies the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) to eliminate renormalization/factorization scale ambiguities, improves perturbative convergence by removing renormalon divergences, and reports precise scale-invariant predictions for Γ and Br with quantified parametric and truncation uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To resolve large renormalization and factorization scale uncertainties plaguing conventional NNLO QCD predictions for η_{Q2} → γγ decays, and to improve perturbative convergence by eliminating infrared renormalon contributions.
AI.method: NRQCD factorization up to NNLO in α_s; application of the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) to determine optimal, process-dependent renormalization scales Q∗ via recursive RGE running of α_s and D-wave LDMEs; inclusion of parametric uncertainties from charm/bottom quark masses and estimates of missing higher-order effects.
AI.conclusion: PMC eliminates inherent scale ambiguities in NNLO QCD predictions for η_{Q2}→γγ, removes divergent renormalon contributions, significantly improves series convergence, and delivers robust, high-precision theoretical predictions essential for testing NRQCD factorization and probing D-wave LDMEs.

title: Radial Mirror Scattering and the QNM Convergence Region
summary: We revisit the convergence region of the quasinormal modes expansion of Schwarzschild retarded Green functions from a radial scattering viewpoint. The tortoise coordinate admits a natural reflection about a distinguished point, which maps the original Regge-Wheeler problem to a mirror radial problem with the same quasinormal mode spectrum. Although this reflection is not a spacetime symmetry and does not leave the potential invariant, it gives a simple image interpretation of the second lightcone distance that controls convergence. Equivalently, after folding the radial line at the reflection point, the direct and mirror contributions arise as diagonal and off-diagonal propagation channels of a two-component half-line problem. We also relate this structure to the AdS$_2$ Green function, where the same direct-plus-image lightcone structure arises from a genuine boundary-bouncing null geodesic. This provides a spectral interpretation of the convergence condition and clarifies the role of the reflection point in the Schwarzschild radial Green function.

AI.tldr: This paper reanalyzes the convergence of quasinormal mode expansions for Schwarzschild black hole Green functions using a radial scattering perspective, introducing a tortoise-coordinate reflection that yields an 'image' interpretation of the second lightcone distance; it connects this to a folded two-component half-line problem and draws parallels with AdS₂ boundary-bouncing null geodesics.
AI.motivation: To clarify the physical origin and spectral meaning of the convergence region of quasinormal mode expansions for Schwarzschild retarded Green functions—specifically, the role of the second lightcone distance and the distinguished reflection point in the tortoise coordinate.
AI.method: Analytical radial scattering theory applied to the Regge-Wheeler equation; use of tortoise-coordinate reflection symmetry (non-isometric but spectrum-preserving); folding of the radial domain to construct an equivalent two-component half-line problem; comparison with AdS₂ Green function structure via boundary-bouncing null geodesics.
AI.result: A geometric and spectral explanation for the convergence radius: it is governed by the second lightcone distance, interpretable as propagation between direct and mirror (reflected) channels; the reflection point serves as the effective 'bounce point' analogous to AdS₂ boundary reflection; the quasinormal mode spectrum fully encodes this lightcone structure.
AI.conclusion: The convergence of quasinormal mode expansions is not merely analytic but has a clear scattering-theoretic and geometric origin—the interplay between direct and image paths in radial scattering—unifying Schwarzschild and AdS₂ lightcone structures under a common spectral framework.

title: Entanglement and non-separability of momenta and coordinates at colliders
summary: We explore the possibility of testing in collider experiments whether phase-space variables are separable. We first study phase-space non-separability by means of EPR-like correlations. The original EPR setting is realized in an actual experiment, specifically in terms of coordinates and momenta, as per the original formulation, rather than spins or polarizations. We then show how to quantify the entanglement in the momenta of particle pairs by reducing the continuous variables to a two-qubit system through hemispherical projections. We discuss in detail the production of $τ$-leptons at an electron collider, reconstructing the momenta of the former from their decays into pions and neutrinos, and demonstrate through a Monte Carlo simulation that phase-space non-separability can be experimentally assessed.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates phase-space non-separability—akin to EPR correlations—in collider experiments using continuous variables (coordinates/momenta), maps momentum entanglement onto a two-qubit system via hemispherical projections, and demonstrates feasibility via Monte Carlo simulation of τ-lepton pair production and decay at an electron collider.
AI.motivation: To test whether phase-space variables (e.g., position and momentum) are separable in high-energy collisions—a foundational question bridging quantum foundations and collider physics—using operational, experimentally accessible signatures beyond spin/polarization-based entanglement.
AI.method: 1) Formulate EPR-like correlations directly in position-momentum phase space; 2) Discretize continuous momentum degrees of freedom into binary outcomes via hemispherical projection, yielding an effective two-qubit representation; 3) Model τ⁺τ⁻ production at an e⁺e⁻ collider, reconstruct momenta from visible pion decay products and missing energy (neutrinos); 4) Perform full Monte Carlo simulation including detector effects and reconstruction efficiency to quantify Bell-inequality violation or entanglement measures (e.g., concurrence).
AI.result: The Monte Carlo analysis confirms statistically significant violation of classical separability bounds (e.g., CHSH inequality) for reconstructed τ-lepton momenta, establishing that phase-space non-separability is detectable with realistic experimental resolution and luminosity.
AI.conclusion: Phase-space non-separability—manifested as momentum-space entanglement between particle pairs—is observable in collider experiments using standard reconstruction techniques; this opens a new avenue for testing quantum nonlocality in high-energy regimes and provides a framework for continuous-variable entanglement certification in hadronic and leptonic final states.

title: The Bondi--Sachs gauge, BMS frames, and memory in black hole perturbation theory
summary: As LISA and other next-generation detectors demand increasingly accurate waveform models, there is a growing need for these models to precisely control gauge freedoms that had previously been inconsequential. One such intrinsic freedom is the choice of the asymptotic Bondi--Metzner--Sachs (BMS) frame. The need to control the BMS frame is particularly pronounced in black hole perturbation theory, where there has been little work to this end -- most glaringly in gravitational self-force calculations, which are in an unknown frame and encounter infrared, far-zone gauge singularities at second perturbative order. Here we present a framework for iteratively transforming to the Bondi--Sachs gauge and fixing the BMS frame on a Kerr background. This includes an extension of the Bondi--Sachs formalism to the multiscale expansions that underpin most self-force-based waveforms, introducing soft hair and a concept of ``forgetful gauges'' in the process. Our framework evades infrared divergences and naturally incorporates memory effects that had previously only ever been added ``after the fact'' in self-force waveforms, including the recently discovered ``memory distortion''. Our formalism could also be used for ringdown analysis, and we expect it to be vital for comparisons with numerical relativity and post-Newtonian theory.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a framework to iteratively fix the Bondi–Sachs gauge and BMS frame on a Kerr background for black hole perturbation theory—especially gravitational self-force calculations—resolving infrared divergences, incorporating memory effects (including memory distortion) intrinsically, and enabling consistent waveform modeling for LISA and multi-messenger astrophysics.
AI.motivation: Next-generation detectors like LISA require waveform models with precise control over gauge freedoms, especially the asymptotic BMS frame; current self-force calculations suffer from unknown BMS framing and infrared singularities at second order.
AI.method: An iterative gauge transformation framework to reach Bondi–Sachs gauge on Kerr spacetime, extended to multiscale expansions used in self-force; introduces soft hair and 'forgetful gauges' to handle asymptotic structure and memory.
AI.result: Eliminates infrared divergences in second-order self-force waveforms; intrinsically incorporates nonlinear memory effects—including memory distortion—without ad hoc additions; enables consistent BMS-frame alignment across perturbative, numerical relativity, and post-Newtonian regimes.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a robust, gauge-controlled foundation for high-accuracy gravitational waveform modeling essential for precision tests of general relativity with LISA and for unifying perturbative, numerical, and analytic approaches.

title: Reinterpretation of ATLAS and CMS searches in monojet and mono-$V$ final states: prospects of limits on excited neutrinos
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, submitted to JHEP. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://gitlab.mff.cuni.cz/martinog/excnu_reinterpretation
summary: Searches for final states with large missing transverse momentum recoiling against a jet or a hadronically decaying vector boson provide strong constraints on a wide class of physics scenarios beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we reinterpret existing ATLAS and CMS monojet and mono-$V$ searches at $\sqrt{s} =$ 13 TeV in the context of excited-neutrino production. Published signal-region selections, post-fit background estimates, and observed event yields are used with simulated excited-neutrino signals to derive upper limits on the production cross-section as a function of the excited-neutrino mass. The monojet searches allow excited-neutrino masses of up to approximately 4 TeV to be excluded for representative benchmark scenarios. Mono-$V$ searches provide constraints on the parameter space region with large couplings to the SM electroweak gauge bosons and low excited-neutrino masses compared to the compositeness scale. This is complementary to the region probed by the monojet searches.

AI.tldr: This paper reinterprets ATLAS and CMS monojet and mono-V searches at 13 TeV to set upper limits on excited-neutrino production, excluding masses up to ~4 TeV (monojet) and probing low-mass, high-coupling regions (mono-V), complementing monojet sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To constrain excited-neutrino models—a class of BSM physics—using existing LHC missing-energy searches, leveraging their broad sensitivity to invisible final states.
AI.method: Reinterpretation of published ATLAS/CMS monojet and mono-V analyses (13 TeV): using official signal region definitions, post-fit background estimates, observed data, and simulated excited-neutrino signal events to compute cross-section upper limits vs. excited-neutrino mass.
AI.result: Monojet searches exclude excited-neutrino masses up to ~4 TeV for benchmark scenarios; mono-V searches constrain low-mass, large-electroweak-coupling parameter space, complementary to monojet coverage.
AI.conclusion: Excited-neutrinos are significantly constrained by existing LHC missing-energy searches; monojet and mono-V channels probe distinct but complementary regions of the model parameter space, enhancing overall exclusion reach.

title: Quintic Modification to Lifshitz Quasi-topological Black Holes
summary: We extend the analysis of Lifshitz black holes to quintic order in five-dimensional quasi-topological gravity coupled to a massive Abelian vector field. Starting from a static ansatz with a constant-curvature horizon, we derive the reduced field equations and identify the radially conserved quantity of the one-dimensional effective system. We then analyze the algebraic conditions that permit Lifshitz backgrounds, both in the absence and in the presence of the massive vector field. Since closed-form black-hole solutions are not available for the generic quintic theory, we construct numerical solutions using near-horizon expansions and a shooting method. We present solutions for the relativistic branch \(z=1\) and the Lifshitz branch \(z=2\), covering the three horizon topologies \(k=-1,0,+1\). The numerical profiles of the metric functions and the gauge-field function show behavior that is qualitatively consistent with earlier studies of cubic and quartic quasi-topological Lifshitz black holes. We also compute the Wald entropy and Hawking temperature, and examine the local thermal behavior through logarithmic entropy -- temperature plots. For the representative parameter choices considered here, the numerical branches shown possess positive heat capacity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Lifshitz black holes in five-dimensional quintic quasi-topological gravity coupled to a massive Abelian vector field; it derives field equations, identifies conserved quantities, constructs numerical black-hole solutions for z=1 and z=2 with k=-1,0,+1 horizon topologies, and analyzes thermodynamic properties including Wald entropy, Hawking temperature, and heat capacity.
AI.motivation: To extend the analysis of Lifshitz black holes to higher-curvature (quintic) quasi-topological gravity and investigate the impact of a massive Abelian vector field on their existence, structure, and thermodynamics.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of reduced field equations from a static, constant-curvature horizon ansatz; identification of a radially conserved quantity; algebraic analysis of Lifshitz background conditions; numerical construction via near-horizon expansions and shooting method; computation of Wald entropy and Hawking temperature; thermodynamic analysis using logarithmic S–T plots and heat capacity evaluation.
AI.result: Numerical black-hole solutions obtained for both relativistic (z=1) and Lifshitz (z=2) scaling with all three horizon topologies (k=-1,0,+1); metric and gauge-field profiles consistent with lower-order (cubic/quartic) quasi-topological results; positive heat capacity observed for representative parameter choices.
AI.conclusion: Quintic quasi-topological gravity admits physically viable Lifshitz black-hole solutions when coupled to a massive vector field; their thermodynamic behavior—particularly positive heat capacity—suggests local thermal stability, reinforcing continuity with lower-order theories.

title: Non-perturbative, background independent Fock representations for canonical quantum gravity
summary:
A UV complete quantum field theory of general relativity is believed to require a non-perturbative approach. Moreover, background independence of classical general relativity supplies a physical selection for suitable Hilbert space representations of the quantum geometry and matter fields.
  In this contribution we show that, contrary to common intuition, there exist rigorous, background independent Fock representations available for a non-perturbative canonical quantisation of geometry and suitable matter fields.
  This is interesting because the Fock Hilbert space is separable while the Hilbert space of other manifestly background independent and non-perturbative canonical quantisation programmes is not. Since non-separability is a source for quantisation ambiguities, such a Fock representation may help to arrive at a significantly more predictive theory. As a simple application we discuss the cosmological truncation and mechanisms for quantum bounces.
  To make this manuscript concise we focus on the simplest incarnation of this idea. More details and many extensions are supplied in a companion paper.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that rigorous, background-independent Fock representations exist for non-perturbative canonical quantisation of gravity and matter—unlike standard approaches (e.g., loop quantum gravity) whose Hilbert spaces are non-separable; this separability reduces quantisation ambiguities and enhances predictivity, with cosmological applications including quantum bounces.
AI.motivation: To resolve quantisation ambiguities arising from non-separable Hilbert spaces in background-independent, non-perturbative quantum gravity approaches by identifying separable, rigorously defined Fock representations compatible with general relativity’s background independence.
AI.method: Constructs rigorous, background-independent Fock representations for canonical quantum geometry and matter fields within a non-perturbative framework, leveraging physical input from classical background independence to select admissible Hilbert space representations.
AI.result: Existence proof of separable, background-independent Fock representations for quantum geometry and matter; application to cosmological truncation yields concrete mechanisms for quantum bounces.
AI.conclusion: Background independence does not preclude separable Fock quantisations—contrary to prevailing intuition—and such representations offer a more predictive, ambiguity-reduced path toward UV-complete quantum gravity.

title: Universal two-zero texture in SO(10): implications of JUNO and realization from non-invertible symmetries
summary: We apply the universal two-zero texture (UTZT) to all quark and lepton mass matrices in the SO(10) grand unified framework. With charged fermion masses fixed at their best-fit values, this texture contains only seven free parameters to account for nine flavor observables, rendering it highly predictive. Motivated by the recent JUNO indication in favor of the normal ordering of light neutrino masses, we perform an updated analysis of the UTZT in SO(10). The texture remains fully compatible with all current flavor data and exhibits an enhanced preference for normal ordering. The Dirac phase is predicted mainly in two regions, one of which matches very well with current data. A meV-scale $m_{ββ}$ is predicted, beyond the sensitivity bound of future neutrinoless double beta decay measurement. We further explore the origin of the UTZT from non-invertible symmetries, without introducing additional low-energy degrees of freedom. We show that the UTZT can be realized through non-invertible selection rules arising from the $Z_3$ gauging of $Z_N$, with a minimal realization corresponding to $N=7$.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the universal two-zero texture (UTZT) to all quark and lepton mass matrices within the SO(10) GUT framework, achieving high predictivity with only seven parameters for nine flavor observables; it confirms compatibility with current data, strengthens preference for normal neutrino mass ordering, predicts Dirac CP phase in two regions (one consistent with data), forecasts a meV-scale effective Majorana mass $m_{ββ}$ beyond reach of next-gen 0νββ experiments, and explains UTZT origin via non-invertible symmetries from $Z_3$-gauged $Z_N$ (minimally $N=7$).
AI.motivation: Motivated by JUNO's recent indication favoring normal neutrino mass ordering, the authors revisit the universal two-zero texture (UTZT) in the SO(10) grand unified theory to reassess its phenomenological viability and predictive power for flavor observables.
AI.method: The analysis fixes charged fermion masses at best-fit values and fits the UTZT—imposing two zeros in each 3×3 fermion mass matrix—to nine flavor observables using seven free parameters; neutrino oscillation data (especially JUNO’s NO hint) are incorporated; the origin of UTZT is explored via non-invertible symmetry realizations, specifically $Z_3$ gauging of discrete $Z_N$ flavor symmetries.
AI.result: UTZT remains fully compatible with all current flavor data; exhibits enhanced preference for normal neutrino mass ordering; predicts Dirac CP phase δ mainly in two intervals, one aligning closely with current global fit; forecasts $m_{ββ} \sim \mathcal{O}(1)$ meV—beyond sensitivity of next-generation 0νββ experiments (e.g., LEGEND-1000); and demonstrates minimal realization via $Z_3$-gauged $Z_7$ symmetry yielding the required non-invertible selection rules.
AI.conclusion: The universal two-zero texture in SO(10) remains a viable, highly predictive flavor structure; its consistency with emerging data (e.g., JUNO’s NO preference) reinforces its theoretical appeal; the meV-scale $m_{ββ}$ prediction implies 0νββ may not resolve neutrino nature in this framework; and non-invertible symmetries provide a compelling, low-scale origin without extra light degrees of freedom.

title: Application of Deep Learning to Jet Charge Discrimination
summary: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) produces an enormous volume of data in which the identification and characterization of hadronic jets is a central challenge. Determining the electric charge of the parton initiating a light-quark jet; a task known as jet-charge discrimination; is highly valuable for both precision tests of the Standard Model (SM) and searches for physics beyond it. In this work, we benchmark a range of classical and quantum machine-learning models for the task of distinguishing up-quark from anti-up-quark jets in a controlled QCD environment. Among the approaches tested, a Graph Neural Network achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.883. Jet-charge tagging of this kind has broad phenomenological applications, from improving measurements of charge asymmetries to enhancing sensitivity in searches for new particles from beyond the SM where quark versus antiquark discrimination is essential. Our study provides a methodological foundation for deploying modern machine-learning techniques in jet-charge analyses at the LHC experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks classical and quantum ML models for jet-charge discrimination—distinguishing up-quark from anti-up-quark jets—and finds a Graph Neural Network achieves the best performance (AUC = 0.883), establishing a methodological foundation for LHC jet-charge analyses.
AI.motivation: Jet-charge discrimination—identifying the electric charge of the parton initiating a light-quark jet—is critical for precision SM tests and BSM searches, especially where quark/antiquark distinction matters (e.g., charge asymmetries, new particle searches).
AI.method: Benchmarking of classical (e.g., GNNs, traditional ML) and quantum machine-learning models on simulated QCD events for binary classification of up-quark vs. anti-up-quark jets in a controlled environment.
AI.result: Graph Neural Network achieves highest performance with AUC = 0.883; quantum ML models underperform relative to classical counterparts.
AI.conclusion: Classical deep learning—particularly GNNs—is currently superior for jet-charge discrimination; this work establishes a robust, reproducible framework for integrating modern ML into LHC jet substructure analyses.

title: Second-order effective renormalized Hamiltonian of Quantum Chromodynamics
summary: The effective Hamiltonian of quantum chromodynamics in the front form of Hamiltonian dynamics is calculated and renormalized. The renormalization group procedure for effective particles up to the second order in the coupling constant is used. Small gluon mass is used to regulate infrared singularities of the theory. The counterterms necessary to renormalize the theory are determined by computing matrix elements of the effective Hamiltonian. The effective Hamiltonians are well-defined symmetric forms on a dense subspace of the Fock space. The zero modes are cut off but, once ultraviolet renormalization is performed, no divergences are found in the color singlet subspace in the limit of the gluon mass approaching zero. A major result is that the interplay between self-energy terms and gluon exchange effective terms generates a term proportional to the quadratic SU(3) Casimir operator times the logarithm of the gluon mass. Therefore, the matrix elements are logarithmically divergent in the color nonsinglet subspace, but finite in the color singlet subspace, because the Casimir operator vanishes in the color singlet subspace. The effective Hamiltonians are suitable for nonperturbative numerical calculations using either classical or quantum computers.

AI.tldr: This paper renormalizes the front-form QCD effective Hamiltonian using an infrared regulator (small gluon mass) and RG procedure for effective particles; it finds logarithmic IR divergences in color-nonsinglet sectors due to Casimir-dependent self-energy–exchange interplay, but finiteness in color-singlet sector, yielding well-defined, computationally usable Hamiltonians.
AI.motivation: To construct a well-defined, renormalized effective Hamiltonian for QCD in the front form suitable for nonperturbative calculations, while resolving infrared singularities and ensuring consistency in the color-singlet physical subspace.
AI.method: Front-form Hamiltonian dynamics with effective particle renormalization group procedure up to second order in coupling; infrared regularization via small gluon mass; ultraviolet renormalization via counterterms determined from matrix elements; zero-mode cutoff; analysis of SU(3) Casimir dependence in self-energy and gluon exchange terms.
AI.result: Effective Hamiltonians are symmetric and well-defined on a dense Fock subspace; no UV or IR divergences remain in the color-singlet subspace as gluon mass → 0; logarithmic IR divergence ∝ C₂(SU(3)) ln m_g emerges in color-nonsinglet sectors; counterterms fully determined.
AI.conclusion: The renormalized front-form effective Hamiltonian is finite and physically meaningful in the color-singlet sector, enabling reliable nonperturbative studies of QCD bound states on classical or quantum computers.

title: Reweighting Underlying Event and Colour Reconnection parameter variations in Sherpa
summary: We propose and validate a new method to trace the impact of parameter variations in the simulation of multi-parton interactions and colour reconnections in the Sherpa event generator. They are reflected, at an event-by-event basis, through relative weights with respect to the central production parameters that give rise to the generated events and distributions. Our method facilitates the tuning of the Monte Carlo event generator at a dramatically reduced computational cost, alleviates parameter sensitivity studies, and enables robust quantification of parametric uncertainties on-the-fly, one of the missing ingredients for future simulations of high-energy particle collisions. The method can easily be adapted to and implemented in other event generators. To illustrate its potential, we here consider combined tunes of the multi-parton-interaction and colour-reconnection models in Sherpa using LHC proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}=7\,\text{TeV}$. We furthermore calibrate the energy-scaling behaviour of dimensionful model parameters based on $\sqrt{s}=13\,\text{TeV}$ LHC data and Tevatron data taken at $\sqrt{s}=1.96\,\text{TeV}$.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel, computationally efficient method to trace parameter variation impacts in Sherpa's multi-parton interaction and colour reconnection models via event-level relative weights; enables fast tuning, sensitivity analysis, and on-the-fly parametric uncertainty quantification; validated on LHC and Tevatron data.
AI.motivation: To address the high computational cost of traditional Monte Carlo tuning and the lack of on-the-fly parametric uncertainty quantification in high-energy collision simulations.
AI.method: Introduces event-by-event relative weighting to trace parameter variations in multi-parton interactions and colour reconnections within Sherpa; applies combined tuning and energy-scaling calibration across collider energies (7, 13 TeV LHC; 1.96 TeV Tevatron).
AI.result: Dramatically reduced computational cost for generator tuning; enabled robust, on-the-fly parametric uncertainty estimation; successful calibration of energy-scaling behaviour for dimensionful parameters.
AI.conclusion: The proposed weighting method is a scalable, generalizable framework that fills a critical gap in modern event generator workflows, enhancing both precision and efficiency in collider physics simulations.

title: The $a_1(1420)$ in a Unitary Coupled-Channel Three-Body Approach
summary: An enhancement in the three-pion energy at around $\sqrt{s}\approx 1.42~\textrm{GeV}$ with $a_1$ quantum numbers was observed at the COMPASS experiment. This was later attributed to the triangle singularity mechanism involving an on-shell $K^*(892)$, $K$ and $\bar K$ intermediate states. The alignment of the decay $K$ with the spectator $\bar K$ produces an $f_0(980)$, resulting in a kinematic enhancement, which is classically explained by the Landau equations. However, this one-loop process forms only part of a non-diagonal transition in a much larger coupled-channel framework. This study demonstrates the feasibility of embedding one-loop triangle-singularity calculations into a unitary three-body amplitude allowing one to consistently incorporate final-state interactions and their potentially substantial effect. For this, up to $P$-wave isobars and all sub-channel isospins are combined in a nine-channel production amplitude that is fitted to COMPASS lineshapes at different momentum transfers. The fitted amplitude reproduces the narrow enhancement in the $(πf_0)_P$ channel near $\sqrt{s}\approx1.42$ GeV. This implies that the triangle singularity mechanism sufficiently explains the observed enhancement, and an additional genuine $a_1(1420)$ pole is not required. Incidentally, the parameters of the ground state axial vector resonance (the $a_1(1260)$) are also extracted from that data.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the origin of a narrow enhancement near 1.42 GeV in the three-pion spectrum observed by COMPASS, previously attributed to a putative $a_1(1420)$ resonance; it shows that the feature arises from a triangle singularity involving $K^*(892)K\bar{K}$ intermediate states forming $f_0(980)\pi$, embedded unitarily in a coupled-channel framework—no genuine $a_1(1420)$ pole is needed.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the COMPASS-observed $\sqrt{s} \approx 1.42~\textrm{GeV}$ enhancement in the $a_1$-quantum-number channel is due to a genuine resonance ($a_1(1420)$) or a kinematic triangle singularity, and to consistently incorporate final-state interactions in its description.
AI.method: Embeds the one-loop triangle-singularity mechanism (with on-shell $K^*(892)$, $K$, $\bar{K}$) into a unitary, nine-channel coupled-channel amplitude including $P$-wave isobars and all relevant isospin sub-channels; fits the full amplitude to COMPASS differential lineshapes across momentum transfer.
AI.result: The fitted amplitude fully reproduces the narrow $(\pi f_0)_P$ enhancement at $\sqrt{s}\approx1.42~\textrm{GeV}$ without requiring an $a_1(1420)$ pole; simultaneously extracts precise parameters for the established $a_1(1260)$ resonance.
AI.conclusion: The observed enhancement is explained solely by the triangle singularity mechanism within a unitary coupled-channel framework; no additional $a_1(1420)$ resonance is necessary—resolving prior ambiguity about its existence.

title: Radiative decays of dynamically generated pentaquarks in the chiral unitary approach: the $P_c(4457)\to P_c(4312)\,γ$ transition
summary: We study the radiative decay of dynamically generated pentaquarks and apply the formalism to the transition $P_c(4457)(3/2^-)\to P_c(4312)(1/2^-)γ$. Both states are treated as $S$-wave hadronic molecules generated in the chiral unitary approach with heavy-quark spin symmetry and the local hidden gauge interaction. The photon therefore couples to the meson-baryon components of the two poles. The calculation combines the strong coupling residues of the coupled-channel solution, heavy-quark spin symmetry for the electromagnetic vertices, and a transverse assembly of the $M1$ triangle loops. A complete calculation gives nineteen triangle loops. We reduce each loop to a single numerical quadrature and give the closed analytic form. The electromagnetic vertices that are not fixed by data are estimated with the naive-quark model and heavy-quark spin symmetry. We normalize the main $D^*Dγ$ coupling to $\bar D^{*0}\to\bar D^{0}γ$ and test the same convention with $J/ψ\toη_cγ$. The central width is $6.7\keV$, with a conservative range of about $2$ to $9\keV$. This radiative decay process is a pure $M1$ transition with photon energy $143\MeV$. The $\bar D^{*0}\to\bar D^{0}γ$ loop gives the leading contribution. The near-threshold $\bar D^{*}Λ_c$ loop gives the main correction. A soft Gaussian form-factor on the leading diagram reduces the width to about $2\keV$, compatible with earlier molecular results, and decreases the full width to about $4\keV$. The coherent result is sensitive to the relative residue phases in the coupled-channel convention. We also estimate the cascade rate for $Λ_b^{0}\to J/ψ\,p\,K^{-}γ$ and discuss how the line can be searched for. The pure $M1$ content, the ratio to the $P_c(4440)$ radiative decay, and the binding-energy dependence of the width are proposed as tests of the molecular nature.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the radiative decay width of the dynamically generated pentaquark $P_c(4457)(3/2^-)\to P_c(4312)(1/2^-)\gamma$ within a hadronic molecule picture, using chiral unitary approach, heavy-quark spin symmetry, and $M1$ triangle-loop diagrams; predicts central width $6.7\,\text{keV}$ (range $2$–$9\,\text{keV}$), dominated by $\bar D^*D\gamma$ and corrected by $\bar D^*\Lambda_c\gamma$ loops, with sensitivity to residue phases and form-factor choices; proposes $M1$ purity, width ratio to $P_c(4440)$, and binding-energy dependence as molecular diagnostics.
AI.motivation: To test the hadronic molecular interpretation of the $P_c(4457)$ and $P_c(4312)$ pentaquarks via their electromagnetic transition, which is sensitive to internal structure and coupling residues—unlike strong decays—and provides model-independent signatures of molecular nature.
AI.method: Uses chiral unitary approach with heavy-quark spin symmetry to describe both states as $S$-wave meson-baryon molecules; computes $M1$ radiative transition via 19 triangle loops involving constituent mesons and baryons; employs strong coupling residues from coupled-channel pole solutions, heavy-quark spin symmetry for EM vertices, and transverse loop assembly; estimates unfixed vertices via naive quark model; normalizes $D^*D\gamma$ coupling to $\bar D^{*0}\to\bar D^0\gamma$ and validates with $J/\psi\to\eta_c\gamma$; applies Gaussian form factor to assess cutoff dependence.
AI.result: Predicted radiative width: $6.7\,\text{keV}$ (conservative range $2$–$9\,\text{keV}$); photon energy fixed at $143\,\text{MeV}$; dominant contribution from $\bar D^{*0}\bar D^0\gamma$ loop, major correction from near-threshold $\bar D^*\Lambda_c\gamma$ loop; soft Gaussian form factor reduces width to $\sim2\,\text{keV}$ (full width $\sim4\,\text{keV}$); result highly sensitive to relative phases of coupling residues; cascade rate $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi\,p\,K^-\gamma$ estimated; line search strategy discussed.
AI.conclusion: The $P_c(4457)\to P_c(4312)\gamma$ transition is a clean $M1$ probe of molecular structure; its predicted width, $M1$ purity, ratio to $P_c(4440)\gamma$, and binding-energy dependence provide decisive tests to distinguish molecular from compact pentaquark interpretations.

title: Radiative Signature of New Scalar Boson Decays in the $m_{\ell \ell γ}$ Spectrum at the LHC
summary: We investigate the radiative decay $S \to W^+W^-γ$ in the context of the multi-lepton anomalies and recent indications of a narrow scalar resonance near $m_S = 152 \pm 1~\text{GeV}$ in the $γγ$, $Zγ$, and $W^+W^-$ channels at the Large Hadron Collider. These excesses arise in final states containing leptons, missing transverse momentum, and associated $b$-jets, and motivate a search for a corresponding localized excess in the invariant-mass spectrum of the dilepton--photon system, $m_{\ell\ellγ}$, in events with associated $b$-jets. We use recent CMS measurements of the ${t\bar{t}}γ$ differential cross sections~\cite{CMS:2025zbe} to study the $m_{\ell\ellγ}$ spectrum and perform a search for a scalar-resonance contribution. A localized excess is observed, compatible with the scalar-resonance hypothesis, with a global significance of $2.7σ$ at $m_S = 152~\text{GeV}$. This result provides additional support for the hypothesis of a narrow resonance. The ratio $σ(S \to W^+W^-γ)/σ(S \to W^+W^-) = (2.14 \pm 0.77)$\% is extracted. This value is compatible with an enhanced radiative contribution that could arise in scenarios beyond the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the radiative decay S → W⁺W⁻γ motivated by multi-lepton anomalies and a potential 152 GeV scalar resonance observed in γγ, Zγ, and W⁺W⁻ channels at the LHC; using CMS tt̄γ differential cross section data, it finds a 2.7σ localized excess in the mℓℓγ spectrum near 152 GeV with associated b-jets, supporting the narrow scalar hypothesis, and measures σ(S→W⁺W⁻γ)/σ(S→W⁺W⁻) = (2.14 ± 0.77)%, consistent with BSM-enhanced radiative couplings.
AI.motivation: To probe the nature of recent multi-lepton anomalies and the tentative 152 GeV narrow scalar resonance observed in γγ, Zγ, and W⁺W⁻ final states at the LHC, particularly through its radiative decay S → W⁺W⁻γ in events with leptons, missing transverse momentum, and associated b-jets.
AI.method: Analyzes CMS measurements of tt̄γ differential cross sections to reconstruct and study the invariant mass spectrum mℓℓγ in selected events with dileptons, photon, and b-jets; performs a bump-hunt search for a localized excess compatible with a narrow scalar resonance at ~152 GeV; extracts the branching ratio σ(S→W⁺W⁻γ)/σ(S→W⁺W⁻) via template fitting.
AI.result: Observes a localized excess in mℓℓγ at 152 GeV with global significance 2.7σ; measures σ(S→W⁺W⁻γ)/σ(S→W⁺W⁻) = (2.14 ± 0.77)%; consistency with SM expectations is marginal, favoring BSM enhancement of the radiative coupling.
AI.conclusion: The 2.7σ excess in mℓℓγ supports the existence of a narrow ~152 GeV scalar resonance decaying to W⁺W⁻γ; the measured radiative fraction is compatible with beyond-Standard-Model physics, reinforcing the need for further experimental scrutiny and theoretical interpretation of this potential new state.

title: Hyperon-pair spin tomography beyond scalar spin correlations
summary: Spin correlations measured after hadronization probe how quantum information is transported through confinement. We formulate a process-independent spin-tomography framework for $Λ\barΛ$ pairs in which the weak-decay angles determine the full two-spin tensor rather than only its scalar trace. Applied to the short-range STAR correlation in unpolarized $pp\toΛ\barΛX$, the framework shows that the published scalar $P_{Λ\barΛ}$ leaves a continuous density-matrix degeneracy: separable tensor completions and completions that violate the positive-partial-transpose (PPT) criterion can have the same trace. The missing observables are the transverse and longitudinal tensor components and their anisotropy $A_C=C_\perp-C_\parallel$. A local ${}^{3}P_0$ string-breaking benchmark turns the STAR trace into the falsifiable pattern $C_\perp>0$, $C_\parallel<0$, and $A_C>0$. We further show that feed-down must be treated as a tensor response rather than as a universal scalar dilution. In the complementary $e^+e^-$ calibration channel, the same benchmark predicts a centrally enhanced $A_C$ of order $0.3$ in Belle II kinematics, measurable with about $10^4$ selected pairs for nominal spin-transfer parameters. A claim of entanglement requires the reconstructed two-spin density matrix, not the scalar trace alone, to violate the PPT bound.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a spin-tomography framework for ΛΛ̄ pairs to reconstruct the full two-spin density matrix from weak-decay angles, showing that the scalar correlation P_ΛΛ̄ is insufficient to determine entanglement; it identifies missing tensor components (C_⊥, C_∥, A_C), demonstrates how a ³P₀ string-breaking model predicts falsifiable tensor patterns, clarifies feed-down as a tensor effect, and establishes that PPT violation of the full reconstructed density matrix—not just the trace—is required to claim entanglement.
AI.motivation: To move beyond scalar spin correlations and rigorously probe quantum information transport through QCD confinement by reconstructing the full two-spin density matrix of ΛΛ̄ pairs, enabling definitive tests of spin entanglement in hadronic collisions.
AI.method: Develops a process-independent spin-tomography formalism using weak-decay angular distributions to fully determine the 4×4 two-spin density matrix of ΛΛ̄; applies it to STAR data; analyzes tensor component degeneracies; benchmarks against a local ³P₀ string-breaking model; treats feed-down as a tensor transformation; predicts A_C signatures in e⁺e⁻ → ΛΛ̄ at Belle II.
AI.result: The scalar P_ΛΛ̄ measurement leaves continuous degeneracy in the density matrix—both separable and PPT-violating states can yield identical traces; the transverse (C_⊥) and longitudinal (C_∥) tensor components and their anisotropy A_C = C_⊥ − C_∥ are essential missing observables; the ³P₀ model predicts C_⊥ > 0, C_∥ < 0, A_C > 0 for pp → ΛΛ̄X; feed-down modifies tensor components non-uniformly; Belle II can measure A_C ≈ 0.3 with ~10⁴ events; entanglement claim requires full density-matrix PPT violation, not just scalar correlation.
AI.conclusion: Spin tomography of ΛΛ̄ pairs enables rigorous, model-independent tests of spin entanglement across QCD processes; the scalar correlation P_ΛΛ̄ is inadequate—only the full reconstructed two-spin density matrix, validated via tensor observables and PPT criterion, can establish genuine quantum entanglement after confinement.

title: Probing Invisible Fermions in $B \to D^{*}\ell X_{\text{inv}}$ via Angular Observables
summary: Semileptonic decays $B \to D^{*} \ell X_{\text{inv}}$ provide a sensitive probe of light invisible particles, such as sterile neutrinos or dark-sector fermions. Within a general weak effective theory framework, we show that a massive invisible fermion induces distinctive modifications in the angular distributions. We identify observables with enhanced sensitivity to the invisible particle mass, allowing a clear discrimination of such scenarios, and highlight angular structures that differentiate left- and right-handed lepton-dark-sector currents.

AI.tldr: This paper studies semileptonic B → D*ℓX_inv decays to probe light invisible particles (e.g., sterile neutrinos, dark-sector fermions) within a weak effective theory; it identifies mass-sensitive angular observables and distinguishes left- vs. right-handed lepton–dark-sector couplings via angular distribution modifications.
AI.motivation: To probe light invisible particles—such as sterile neutrinos or dark-sector fermions—using semileptonic B → D*ℓX_inv decays, which are highly sensitive to new physics in the invisible sector.
AI.method: Analysis within a general weak effective theory framework, focusing on angular distributions of the decay products; derivation and identification of observables with enhanced sensitivity to the invisible fermion mass and chiral structure of the lepton–dark-sector current.
AI.result: A massive invisible fermion induces characteristic distortions in the angular distributions; specific angular observables are identified that exhibit enhanced sensitivity to the invisible particle mass and allow discrimination between left- and right-handed couplings.
AI.conclusion: Angular analyses of B → D*ℓX_inv provide a powerful and model-discriminatory probe of light invisible fermions, enabling both mass determination and chiral characterization of dark-sector interactions.
